They may share one review, but the reviewer needs to distinguish them. The code changes behavior. The format changes how information is stored. The criteria may change what completion means. CyberAlchemy Lab records each intended effect so an owner can see what is being accepted.
entries.editorial: The investigation suggests revised code, a different record format and new success criteria. Reviewing them together is convenient, provided the owner can distinguish their effects. Code changes behavior. A format changes stored representation. Criteria might change completion’s meaning. The Lab records the intended effects before acceptance.

entries.original: Lifecycle describes states and permitted changes through time. Different things have different lifecycles. The Lab can accept a record format while a particular record using it remains a draft. It can select software before activating it. A graph can actively represent a proposed source while preserving its proposed status. An agent session can end while the project continues. No single status answers all these questions.
entries.editorial: Lifecycle gives each subject its states and permitted changes over time. A record format can be accepted while a particular record is still a draft. Selected software can await activation. A graph can represent a proposal as proposed. A session ends while its project continues. We need each subject’s state to understand those facts.

entries.original: The Lab names three distinct kinds of change. A Semantic Epoch is an owner-selected version of the accepted meaning: an owner-determined material change to the rule for which rows belong in an export requires a successor meaning version. A Representation Revision changes the designated machine encoding or format while preserving meaning, with explicit equivalence evidence, validation and owner selection. A Derived Refresh regenerates and validates a human-readable or lookup view from unchanged canonical input under an exact generator binding. It creates no new meaning, representation revision, decision or authority effect. Changing the generator follows its own tooling process. These distinctions prevent a formatting change from silently altering a rule.
entries.editorial: The Lab separates three changes. A Semantic Epoch is an owner-selected accepted meaning version; a material owner-determined change to export inclusion rules needs a successor. A Representation Revision changes machine encoding while preserving meaning, with equivalence evidence, validation and owner selection. A Derived Refresh regenerates and validates a view from unchanged canonical input under an exact generator binding. It adds no meaning, representation revision, decision or authority effect. A generator change follows its tooling route.

entries.original: A proposal identifies the things and versions concerned, exact file contents where relevant, requested effects, authority limits and conditions that would make it invalid. A Decision selects an outcome within those limits. A Decision Bundle presents distinct decisions at one checkpoint—a place where the person reviews them together. Each decision retains its owner, targets and permitted effects. Accepting one does not automatically accept the others.
entries.editorial: A proposal identifies exact subjects, versions and relevant file bytes, requested effects, authority limits and invalidating conditions. A Decision chooses an outcome within those limits. A Decision Bundle puts separate decisions at one review checkpoint. Their owners, targets and effects stay separate, so accepting one supplies no automatic acceptance for the rest.

entries.original: An Admission Transaction applies an already authorized bundle. Admission means formal acceptance for a stated purpose and scope. The transaction checks the authorization, targets and input state, then applies the declared consequences together. These can include accepted records, receipts, history entries, updated Project State and generated indexes. Project State is the project’s saved records and knowledge outside any agent. The transaction adds no permission beyond the decisions it applies.
entries.editorial: An Admission Transaction applies an already authorized bundle. It checks authorization, targets and starting state, then applies the declared consequences together. Accepted records, receipts, histories, Project State and generated indexes can be part of that result. Project State is saved knowledge outside any agent. The transaction has only the permission supplied by its decisions.

entries.original: The inspected records show this arrangement in use. One governance approval covered record-type contracts, the Admission Transaction definition and connection-rule changes. Their consequences were applied together. A later approval accepted the local runtime implementation—the software performing selected Lab operations—and its declared operational records. Each approval identifies its scope. Deployment and publication have their own authorization requirements.
entries.editorial: The inspected records show a governance approval covering record contracts, the Admission Transaction definition and connection rules, with consequences applied together. A later approval accepted the local runtime and declared operational records. Each approval identifies its scope. Deployment and publication still have their own authorization requirements.

entries.original: Two histories retain separate accounts of the result. Project Semantic Event History records complete resulting project states and their predecessors: what changed. Project Governance Event History records the decisions, authorization, policies, challenge rules and evidence for those particular changes: why they were accepted. Both identify the same specific change events so a reader can join the accounts without confusing their roles.
entries.editorial: Two histories let us recover the result. Project Semantic Event History records complete resulting states and predecessors. Project Governance Event History records decisions, authorization, policies, challenges and evidence for those changes. Both identify the same change events, letting a reader connect what changed with why it was accepted.

entries.original: Event sourcing is the engineering idea of retaining an ordered change history and reconstructing state from it. Replay performs that reconstruction from recorded inputs. The Lab adds a separately linked history of authority. Reconstructing a state does not itself decide whether its inputs were accepted under the applicable rules. Martin Fowler, Event Sourcing .
entries.editorial: Event sourcing retains an ordered change history and reconstructs state from it. Replay performs that reconstruction from recorded inputs. The Lab also links a separate authority history. Reconstructing a state leaves the acceptance of its inputs to the applicable governance records.

entries.original: The local implementation demonstrates a limited form of this mechanism. A signed proposal identifies the intended changes and expected starting state. An exclusive writer lock prevents competing local writes; prepared transaction records are retained before the reference to accepted state is updated. Recovery distinguishes completed history from recognized unfinished work. The recorded evidence concerns interruption of a local process on the selected filesystem. It does not establish durability after power loss or coordination across machines.
entries.editorial: The local implementation supplies bounded evidence. A signed proposal identifies changes and expected starting state. An exclusive writer lock prevents competing local writes. Prepared transaction records precede the accepted-state reference update, and recovery recognizes completed history and unfinished work. The recorded tests concern local process interruption on the selected filesystem, without establishing power-loss durability or coordination across machines.

entries.original: A Challenge Contract specifies who may contest a revision, acceptable reasons and evidence, who responds, timing and resolution requirements. A Challenge Event records a particular eligible challenge. For example, missing-row evidence can challenge an export-completeness finding. Filing it creates a matter that the contract requires someone to resolve. Suspension, withdrawal or a changed meaning still requires the applicable rule and an authorized decision.
entries.editorial: A Challenge Contract sets eligible participants, reasons, evidence, responsibility, timing and resolution requirements. A Challenge Event records one eligible challenge. Missing-row evidence could challenge a completeness finding. Filing it creates a matter requiring resolution. Suspension, withdrawal or revised meaning still needs the applicable rule and authorized decision.

entries.original: After an accepted change, the next agent may need different information. A Context View is information selected for a task, with source versions and conditions for its use identified. A view prepared before the change can become stale. The runtime can require a new selection tied to the accepted state before work continues. The agent recovers the change and its authority from project records rather than relying on a remembered conversation.
entries.editorial: An accepted change can leave an earlier Context View stale. The view identifies task information, source versions and use conditions. The runtime can require a fresh checked selection tied to accepted state. The next agent recovers the change and authority from project records, with no need to inherit a private conversation.

entries.original: A software company wants customers to export their data reliably. CyberAlchemy Lab records that desired outcome and its constraints as an Intent before choosing a solution. Intent Resolution records the owner’s selected response and how success will be assessed. The response may be a product improvement, a particular project or a research question. Choosing it supplies direction; it does not establish delivery.
entries.editorial: A software company wants customers to export data reliably. Intent records the outcome and constraints before a solution is chosen. Intent Resolution records the owner’s response and success assessment. That response might be product work, a project or a research question. Choosing it gives direction, with delivery still to establish.

entries.original: The Product is the continuing offering, such as the customer platform. Its Product Thesis explains who it serves, the problem addressed, the expected value and which propositions still need evidence. A Product Capability states an outcome it should enable, such as reliable export. A service, command or agent workflow may provide that outcome, but each technical realization has its own identity and lifecycle.
entries.editorial: The Product is the continuing offering, such as the customer platform. Its Product Thesis explains the audience, problem, value and propositions needing evidence. A Product Capability states an outcome such as reliable export. A service, command or agent workflow could realize it, each with its own identity and lifecycle.

entries.original: A Capability Realization Binding is the record linking a specific capability version to specific implementation versions and their roles. It also records compatibility, ownership, adoption status and conditions for replacement. Several implementations can participate. Changing that association can preserve the capability’s identity while changing delivery. The link itself does not prove adoption, installation, activation, compliance with requirements or customer benefit; each needs the applicable decision or evidence.
entries.editorial: A Capability Realization Binding links specific capability and implementation versions, roles, compatibility, ownership, adoption posture and replacement conditions. Several implementations can participate, and delivery can change while the capability keeps its identity. The binding leaves adoption, installation, activation, conformance and customer benefit to the appropriate decision or evidence.

entries.original: A Project organizes a declared effort toward a purpose. It records scope, exclusions, goals, responsibility, evidence and lifecycle. The export-repair project might have a Goal of no required rows omitted under a specified comparison. A Work record identifies one activity, its inputs, participants, expected result and constraints. A successful work item can contribute to the goal; the goal’s conditions and owner-controlled status change still determine whether it is achieved.
entries.editorial: A Project organizes an effort with purpose, scope, exclusions, goals, responsibility, evidence and lifecycle. Its export-repair Goal might require no omitted identifiers under a selected comparison. Work names a bounded activity and its inputs, participants, result and constraints. That activity can contribute to the Goal, whose conditions and owner-controlled state change still govern achievement.

entries.original: The platform can continue after the repair project finishes. The project can also investigate several implementations without committing the product to any of them. Project membership, adoption of an implementation and demonstrated product value are separately recorded facts. Their distinction lets later work recover what was investigated, selected and observed.
entries.editorial: The platform continues beyond the repair Project. The Project can examine several implementations before any product adoption. Membership, adoption and demonstrated value therefore need separate records. Later work can recover what was investigated, selected and observed.

entries.original: A Method describes a repeatable way to transform inputs into results, with actions, roles, checkpoints and treatment of unresolved work. A Craft Method specializes this into construction that can be divided into smaller governed tasks and recombined. Define makes behavior and limits explicit; Design chooses an arrangement; Plan specifies how the work will proceed. Each resulting record uses the contracts selected for that work.
entries.editorial: A Method describes repeatable transformation of inputs into results, with actions, roles, checkpoints and unresolved work. A Craft Method specializes construction into smaller governed tasks and their recombination. Define makes behavior and limits explicit. Design selects an arrangement; Plan describes how work proceeds. The resulting records use the selected contracts.

entries.original: An Implementation identifies a technical realization, its sources, interfaces, build or deployment materials and evidence. A Workflow orders operations and identifies their connections, decisions and recovery handling. Construction continues through conformance—showing that a particular result meets particular requirements—operation, recovery and later change. Smaller construction tasks need their own owners, a way to recombine results and a stopping condition. Residue records meaningful unfinished or unpreserved work.
entries.editorial: Implementation identifies a technical realization with sources, interfaces, build or deployment materials and evidence. Workflow orders software Operations and their connections, decisions and recovery. Construction continues through conformance, operation, recovery and later change. Smaller tasks need owners, recombination and stop conditions. Residue keeps meaningful unfinished or unpreserved work visible.

entries.original: A Coordination Context is a saved frame for what the work concerns and why information is needed. It is anchored to exactly one Product and can optionally identify one Project and one primary Goal. The selected successor contract preserves that structure. A project may have several goals, while a goal-focused context keeps its chosen primary goal. A material change to Product, Project, Goal or purpose requires a successor context identity. It also records intended consumers and rules for selecting sources.
entries.editorial: A Coordination Context saves why information is needed and what the work concerns. It has exactly one Product anchor and optionally one Project and one primary Goal. A Project might have several goals while this context selects one. A material change to those anchors or purpose needs a successor context identity. Consumers and source-selection rules belong in the record too.

entries.original: A Bounded Context defines a part of a domain within which terms have a consistent meaning. Sales and billing may both say “customer” while distinguishing different facts. A Context Map records the directional relationships between particular versions of those models. This is the domain-driven design concern with coherent local meaning and explicit relationships between models. Martin Fowler, Bounded Context .
entries.editorial: Sales and billing might both use “customer” while referring to different facts. A Bounded Context establishes consistent local meaning, and a Context Map records directional relationships between particular model versions. Domain-driven design gives a useful account of those coherent meanings and explicit model connections.

entries.original: A Context Profile supplies reusable rules for constructing and resolving contexts; it is not itself a particular context. A Context Request states what an identified task or consumer needs, including selection and freshness requirements. A Context View is the resulting fixed selection, with exact sources, exclusions and expiry. The saved context, reusable rules, request and generated view have separate identities. Refreshing information does not silently redefine the purpose it serves.
entries.editorial: A Context Profile supplies reusable construction and resolution rules. A Context Request identifies task or consumer needs, selection and freshness. A Context View supplies the fixed result with exact sources, exclusions and expiry. These records keep separate identities, so a refresh leaves the purpose to its own governing change route.

entries.original: Project State is the saved project knowledge: records, definitions, connections, decisions, evidence and histories. A Ledger is an ordered collection with explicit entry, integrity, correction and reconciliation rules. Some event histories add append-only rules—earlier entries are retained—and support reconstruction from events. The general Ledger definition does not make every collection immutable or every entry true, accepted or authoritative.
entries.editorial: Project State retains records, definitions, connections, decisions, evidence and histories. A Ledger is an ordered collection with entry, integrity, correction and reconciliation rules. Some histories add append-only requirements and event reconstruction. The general Ledger meaning makes no blanket claim that every collection is immutable or every entry true, accepted or authoritative.

entries.original: These responsibilities connect the customer need to results that later work can inspect. The export agent can find the intended outcome, product capability, remaining project conditions, selected method, software and evidence. The library provides the exact definitions and record requirements. Readers can follow that path without first memorizing the identifiers used to link its parts.
entries.editorial: The export agent now has a route through the need, capability, remaining project conditions, method, software and evidence. The reference library supplies exact meanings and record requirements. We can follow that route while learning the identifiers along the way.

entries.original: “The experiment evaluates the export capability” sounds clear in conversation. A system record needs more precision: which experiment design or run, and which capability version? Does the link say what was evaluated, that evidence supports a claim, or that software was adopted? CyberAlchemy Lab keeps these meanings separate so following one connection does not accidentally answer another question.
entries.editorial: “The experiment evaluates the export capability” works in conversation. For a record, we need to identify the design or run and capability version. We also need to distinguish evaluation from evidence support or software adoption. Each connection should answer its own question.

entries.original: A Definition states a term’s accepted meaning within an owner’s scope. Its scientific and formal wording governs that meaning; its plain-language and domain explanations help readers understand it. An Artifact Type sets requirements for records of a particular kind, linking meanings to a versioned machine format and its other required views. An artifact instance is one particular identifiable, versioned record. Accepting a type and accepting a record using it are separate authority acts. The Lab calls formal acceptance admission.
entries.editorial: A Definition governs meaning within its owner’s scope through scientific and formal wording. Plain-language and domain voices explain it. An Artifact Type governs the record kind’s machine format and required views. An artifact instance identifies a particular versioned record. Type acceptance and instance acceptance are separate admissions.

entries.original: A Schema specifies permitted structure: kinds, fields, constraints and connection rules. A record that passes schema checks meets those checked structural requirements. Its evidence can still be weak, sources outdated or requested actions unauthorized. W3C SHACL illustrates how graph-structure checks can be explicit. This comparison explains one validation task; it does not establish that the Lab uses SHACL or that passing structure checks accepts a record’s meaning. W3C SHACL .
entries.editorial: A Schema states structural requirements, including kinds, fields, constraints and connections. Passing its checks leaves evidence strength, source freshness and action permission to other records. W3C SHACL illustrates explicit graph-structure checking. This comparison establishes neither Lab use of SHACL nor acceptance through a structural pass.

entries.original: The Four-Facet Artifact Invariant applies to governed actions that create, change, route, validate, promote, implement or interpret load-bearing artifacts, state or meaning. Before such an action can govern downstream work, it must bind, create or record a missing facet as typed residue for each of four aspects: classification, schema, a view a human can understand and continue from, and a view a machine can parse or check. Missing aspects need their reason, owner, evidence and an explicit continue, defer or block outcome. The Canonical Representation Invariant separately requires one designated machine representation. “Canonical” here concerns its declared form and origin; it does not itself mean true or authoritative. Human explanations and convenience labels must not become competing master records.
entries.editorial: The Four-Facet Artifact Invariant applies to governed actions on load-bearing artifacts, state or meaning. Before downstream governance, the action must bind, create or record typed residue for classification, schema, a human continuation view and a machine-readable view. Missing facets need reason, owner, evidence and a continue, defer or block outcome. The Canonical Representation Invariant separately designates one machine representation. That designation concerns form and origin, without itself proving truth or authority.

entries.original: Registries are catalogs selecting exact definitions and record contracts. Artifact Type Resolution identifies an accepted contract from an exact reference or a declared discriminator—a field and value that identify the type. It reports uncertainty or ambiguity instead of guessing from filenames. Older references may still resolve while another version is selected as current. If no reusable contract fits, an Artifact Type Request records the gap for review. The request is not a substitute for the missing accepted type.
entries.editorial: Registries select exact definitions and contracts. Artifact Type Resolution uses an exact reference or declared discriminator, reporting ambiguity instead of guessing from filenames. An older reference can resolve while a newer version is current. An Artifact Type Request records a reusable-contract gap for review, without supplying the missing accepted contract.

entries.original: A Relation Kind defines one kind of connection, its direction, permitted source–target kind pairs, required extra details and conclusions the link cannot justify. A Typed Relation is one connection between specific versions under that rule. The snapshot’s catalog contains 41 relation kinds and 550 allowed ordered pairs. “Ordered” means source and target are not interchangeable. A list of possible sources and targets does not permit every combination.
entries.editorial: A Relation Kind declares meaning, direction, permitted ordered endpoint pairs, required details and inference limits. A Typed Relation instantiates the rule between specific versions. This snapshot has 41 kinds and 550 permitted ordered pairs. Source and target are not interchangeable, and separate lists do not permit every possible combination.

entries.original: For example, member-of records membership, contributes-to records intended contribution, and evaluates identifies what was assessed. evidence-bears-on records how evidence relates to a claim, including the stated direction of support or opposition. These links cannot replace one another. The catalog explicitly permits Experiment Design and Experiment Run to evaluate Product, Product Capability, Product Thesis and Capability Realization Binding. Experiments therefore have permitted product connections as well as research connections; none implies a favorable result.
entries.editorial: Membership, intended contribution, evaluation and evidence support need different connections. member-of, contributes-to, evaluates and evidence-bears-on record those facts, including support or opposition where required. Experiment Design and Experiment Run may evaluate Product, Product Capability, Product Thesis and Capability Realization Binding. Product connections are available alongside research connections, with no promised favorable outcome.

entries.original: The Typed Connection Extension Rule specifies how permitted connections can expand. Reuse an existing relation kind when its meaning and constraints fit. Adding a source–target pair requires review and acceptance of a revised contract. Asking a different semantic question requires a distinct relation kind. The process preserves ownership, evidence, versions, lifecycle and challenge rights. Registering a new kind of endpoint—the thing at either end of a connection—does not grant it additional connections.
entries.editorial: The Typed Connection Extension Rule governs expansion. Reuse a fitting meaning and constraints. An additional ordered pair needs review and an accepted successor contract; a different semantic question needs a distinct relation kind. Ownership, evidence, versions, lifecycle and challenge rights remain explicit. Registering an endpoint kind grants no extra connections.

entries.original: Non-collapse checks whether concepts describe genuinely different facts. An assignment can exist before permission is delegated. A capability can be declared before an implementation is adopted. An experiment can evaluate a product and fail. Formalization translates these distinctions into logical statements. A witness or countermodel is a specified case demonstrating the distinction under stated assumptions. Consistency checks instead ask whether the combined requirements can all hold together within the chosen theory.
entries.editorial: Non-collapse asks whether concepts describe different facts. Assignment can precede delegation, capability can precede adoption, and evaluation can fail. Formalization expresses those distinctions logically. A witness or countermodel demonstrates a distinction under assumptions. Consistency asks whether the combined requirements hold together in the selected theory.

entries.original: The inspected assurance work covers sources for 183 selected definition identities and contains partial formal translations. It reports zero verified whole-definition proofs at that snapshot. A proof checker can accept a formal statement while the relationship between that statement and the intended definition still needs justification. Lean’s documentation helps explain that boundary. A successful check supports a claim about the Lab only with an adequate account of how the formal statement represents its source meaning. Lean, Validating a Lean Proof .
entries.editorial: The inspected assurance work covers sources for 183 selected definition identities and partial translations. It reports zero verified whole-definition proofs. A proof checker’s accepted statement still needs a justified relationship to the intended definition. Lean’s documentation explains that boundary. A Lab claim requires adequate evidence connecting the formal statement to its source meaning.

entries.original: An ontology is a structured model of concepts, things and relationships. An Ontology Node represents a specific thing and revision. An Ontology Edge represents a particular Typed Relation or a connection explicitly declared within that ontology. A local connection does not become a global Lab relation merely by appearing in the graph. Representations and source records retain separate identities and authority; drawing an edge cannot authorize changing the source.
entries.editorial: An ontology organizes concepts, things and relationships. A Node represents a specific subject and revision. An Edge represents a Typed Relation or an explicitly declared local connection. Local appearance does not make a connection global. Graph and source identities stay separate, and drawing an edge supplies no authority to change its source.

entries.original: A Model Instance Binding similarly records how a local instance relates to a particular shared parent model while keeping their owners and authority separate. An Ontology Cut reconstructs one consistent recorded state from selected positions in its event histories. An Ontology View selects from that state for a purpose. A graph answering “what relates to lifecycle?” must identify its sources, coverage, exclusions, unresolved references and freshness. Completeness is measured against that stated scope, not every possible project object.
entries.editorial: A Model Instance Binding links a local instance to a shared parent model while preserving owners and authority. An Ontology Cut reconstructs a consistent state from selected event-history positions; a View selects from it for a purpose. A lifecycle graph needs sources, coverage, exclusions, unresolved references and freshness. Completeness is assessed within that scope.

entries.original: A new AI agent starts the export investigation on Monday. It has no private recollection of last week’s review. It needs the selected software, current evidence, project goal and permission to use tools. CyberAlchemy Lab organizes those inputs into an explicit session—a temporary working period for one machine-agent instance—while saving useful project knowledge outside the agent.
entries.editorial: A new agent starts the export investigation on Monday. Last week’s review is unavailable as private recollection. The agent needs selected software, current evidence, the project goal and tool permission. The Lab prepares an explicit session for one temporary machine instance and saves useful knowledge outside it.

entries.original: Actor is the general classification for an identifiable participant. A Person is a human; a Team is a continuing group; a Principal is an identity recognized for authentication, authorization, ownership or accountability at a particular boundary. A Role describes a position; Responsibility describes what a participant must answer for. Team Membership and Role Assignment record belonging and role occupancy separately. References point to these identities without making a person, account and role the same thing.
entries.editorial: Actor classifies identifiable participants. Person, Team and Principal identify a human, continuing group and boundary-recognized identity respectively. Principals support authentication, authorization, ownership or accountability. Role describes a position; Responsibility describes what someone answers for. Team Membership and Role Assignment record separate facts. A reference leaves person, account and role identities distinct.

entries.original: Agent classifies an operational actor. An Agent Profile records reusable behavior, inputs, outputs, tools, evidence, escalation and stopping conditions. An Agent Capability describes a class of attempts the agent can technically make, including input, output and failure requirements. An Agent Instance is one concrete realization, with its profile, implementation, capabilities and accountability identified. Concrete participant kinds have their own records; the model does not require a duplicate universal Actor record for each one.
entries.editorial: Agent classifies an operational actor. Its Profile supplies reusable behavior, inputs, outputs, tools, evidence, escalation and stop conditions. An Agent Capability describes technically possible attempts and their input, output and failure requirements. An Instance identifies a concrete realization and accountability. Concrete participant kinds use their own records without requiring a duplicate universal Actor record.

entries.original: An Agent Assignment identifies expected participation in particular work, intent, project, goal, run, role or responsibility, with limits and deliverables. Delegation separately records permission from an authorized owner or principal. For the export, the job might be to diagnose missing rows while permission covers only reading selected sources and proposing a fix. Customer communication and production changes remain excluded. Knowing what to do and being allowed to do it are different facts.
entries.editorial: Assignment identifies expected participation in work, intent, project, goal, run, role or responsibility, with limits and deliverables. Delegation separately grants scoped permission. Diagnosing an export might permit reading selected material and proposing a fix while excluding customer communication and production changes. The job and permission need separate records.

entries.original: Saltzer and Schroeder’s least-privilege principle confines a program or user to the permissions needed for its work. Complete mediation calls for checking authorization whenever access occurs, including relevant changes to earlier permissions. These principles explain why an old instruction cannot indefinitely authorize actions. They provide design guidance; they do not demonstrate enforcement on every Lab execution path. Basic Principles of Information Protection .
entries.editorial: Saltzer and Schroeder describe least privilege and complete mediation: limit permissions to the work and check authorization whenever access occurs, including relevant changes to earlier grants. Those principles help explain why an old instruction has limits. They provide design guidance rather than evidence of enforcement on every Lab path.

entries.original: An Agent Session identifies one instance and assignment, its Context and Ontology Views, policies, permissions, inputs, resource limits and termination conditions. A machine instance belongs to one session and ends with it. Profiles and historical session records can persist in project records. The operating machine worker and its working memory are temporary; they do not continue privately across sessions.
entries.editorial: A Session binds one instance and assignment to Context and Ontology Views, policies, permissions, inputs, budgets and termination conditions. The machine instance belongs to that session and ends with it. Profiles and historical session records can persist. The operating worker and its working memory are temporary.

entries.original: Project State supplies saved knowledge: records, definitions, decisions, evidence, histories and connections. Every included record retains its own standing; inclusion in an accepted state does not by itself accept a proposal or promote a source. A Context Request asks for what this session needs. A Context View supplies a fixed selection, identifying sources, versions and use conditions. An Ontology View supplies a selected connected model from a consistent recorded state, called a cut. Together they provide task information and relevant relationships while retaining the authority limits of their sources.
entries.editorial: Project State supplies saved knowledge with each record’s standing intact. Including a proposal in an accepted state does not accept the proposal. A Context Request identifies session needs; a Context View gives a fixed source selection with versions and use conditions. An Ontology View supplies a connected selection from a consistent cut. Both retain source authority limits.

entries.original: Session Memory holds temporary notes, intermediate alternatives and reminders for one session. It ends when that session terminates. A useful note can be proposed as a saved reflection, evidence record or lesson through the applicable record and approval process. Retaining a private note is not the same as adding it to Project State. A future agent reconstructs its position from saved records and newly prepared views.
entries.editorial: Session Memory holds temporary notes, alternatives and reminders, then ends with the session. Useful material can enter the applicable reflection, evidence or lesson route. A private note has to follow the recording process before becoming Project State. Later agents recover their position through saved records and fresh views.

entries.original: The inspected local runtime implements a limited version of this contract. Notes stay in process memory, have an entry limit and are cleared on closure. The session identifies the selected accepted-state reference, source selection and expiry time. A changed state reference, changed source digest—the file’s content fingerprint—or expired interval invalidates the context for continued use. The response is to prepare and check current context through the applicable process.
entries.editorial: The inspected local runtime keeps bounded notes in process memory and clears them on closure. A session records accepted-state reference, source selection and expiry. Changed state reference, changed source digest or expiry invalidates continued context use. The agent needs current checked context through the applicable route.

entries.original: An exported context packet is a saved result of preparation, not a continuing session credential. The runtime’s context-only export closes the session after preparing that packet. A later consumer must establish the information freshness and permissions needed for its own session. Keeping the file does not keep the earlier machine instance alive or preserve its expired permissions.
entries.editorial: A saved context packet is an output of preparation. The runtime’s context-only export closes its session after preparing that packet. A later consumer needs its own freshness and permission checks. Keeping the file preserves neither the earlier machine instance nor expired grants.

entries.original: An Agent Action records who proposed, attempted, completed, rejected or failed an operation, with its session and relevant inputs. A Tool provides a versioned interface for invoking an operation. Tool availability, technical capability, the recorded action and an observed effect are separate facts. A Work Outcome Assessment compares an expected result with the result observed; it does not automatically prove wider benefit.
entries.editorial: Agent Action records attributable proposals, attempts, completion, rejection or failure, with session and inputs. A Tool supplies a versioned invocation interface. Availability, ability, action and observed effect are different facts. A Work Outcome Assessment compares expected and observed results within its scope.

entries.original: The agent can now prepare current information, inspect its job and permissions, choose permitted tools, record actions and produce results with evidence and unresolved work. Proposed changes to saved project records follow their required review and authorization process. After closure, another agent can inspect the accepted results through new views without inheriting private memory or unrestricted permissions from its predecessor.
entries.editorial: The agent can recover current information, inspect assignment and permission, choose allowed tools and record actions, evidence and unresolved work. Proposed Project State changes follow review and authorization. After closure, another agent recovers accepted results through new views without inheriting private memory or unrestricted grants.

entries.original: An export fix works for the original customer, then fails for a larger account. An AI agent proposes advice: compare adjacent data batches before reporting success. Retrieving data in successive batches is called pagination. In CyberAlchemy Lab, advice for later work needs supporting evidence, use conditions, a predicted benefit and a result that could contradict it. Saving the sentence preserves it. Examining later use establishes whether it helps.
entries.editorial: In a separate hypothetical episode, an export fix works for the original customer and later fails for a larger account. The agent suggests comparing adjacent batches before reporting success. Retrieving those batches is pagination. Advice for future work needs evidence, conditions, predicted benefit and a result contradicting the prediction. Saving it preserves the advice. Later use tells us whether it helps.

entries.original: The Operational Learning Cycle starts with work whose participants and conditions can be identified. Sessions and actions produce results, feedback, measurements and residue—meaningful unresolved or unpreserved work. An Operational Observation records ordinary-work information; Observation is the distinct record kind used during a Research or Experiment Run. An Agent Reflection records a revisable diagnostic interpretation. It can identify a suspected mistake or useful practice for investigation. It is a report suitable for review, not a requirement to save private internal reasoning.
entries.editorial: The Operational Learning Cycle starts with identifiable work, participants and conditions. Sessions and actions yield results, feedback, measurements and residue. Operational Observation records ordinary-work information; research and experiment runs use Observation. Agent Reflection records a revisable diagnostic interpretation for review. It is a report, without requiring retention of private internal reasoning.

entries.original: An Operational Lesson makes that advice precise. It could apply to exports retrieved in batches while the dataset changes, excluding fixed-data exports with a different integrity contract. It predicts that the check will detect missing rows before delivery. Its falsifier is a result contradicting that prediction: the check misses the known failure or rejects valid output without useful detection. The advice remains limited to the conditions its evidence supports.
entries.editorial: An Operational Lesson makes the advice specific. Here it could apply while data changes between batch requests, excluding fixed-data exports with a different integrity contract. It predicts detection before delivery. A falsifier would show the check missing the known failure or rejecting valid output without useful detection. The evidence bounds the advice.

entries.original: A Lesson Application records use or deliberate non-use of a specific lesson version in later work. Showing it to an agent, selecting it, using it, following it correctly and obtaining a successful outcome are distinct facts. A Lesson Outcome Assessment examines the predicted benefit and contradicting conditions against observed results. A Work Outcome Assessment instead asks what the task achieved. Completing an export does not alone show that a lesson caused improvement.
entries.editorial: Lesson Application records actual use or deliberate non-use of an exact version. Presentation, selection, use, correct use and success are different facts. Lesson Outcome Assessment examines predicted benefit and contradicting conditions against observations. Work Outcome Assessment asks what the task achieved. A completed export leaves the lesson’s causal contribution to be assessed.

entries.original: A Research Inquiry records a question and its scope, source rules, method and stopping conditions. A Research Run records what an investigation actually did. A Hypothesis states a testable proposition. An Experiment Design states the planned conditions, variables, comparisons, measurements and stop rules. An Experiment Run records execution, deviations and observations. A plan, its execution and favorable results have separate records.
entries.editorial: Research Inquiry records a scoped question with sources, method and stopping conditions. Research Run records the investigation. Hypothesis states a testable proposition. Experiment Design declares conditions, variables, comparisons, measurements and stop rules; Experiment Run records execution, deviations and observations. Planning, execution and favorable outcomes each need their own account.

entries.original: An experiment may address research, evaluate a product proposition or assess an implementation’s relationship to a capability. The connection catalog states which record kinds may connect, in which direction. For the export, runs could compare dataset sizes and concurrent changes using an identified counting method. An evaluates connection records what was assessed. Evidence connections record how results bear on a claim. A Finding states the conclusion and its limits.
entries.editorial: Experiments can address research, product propositions or implementation-capability relationships under declared endpoint and direction rules. For exports, runs could compare dataset size and concurrent changes with an identified method. evaluates records the assessed subject. Evidence connections describe claim support, and a Finding states the bounded conclusion.

entries.original: Failure records also separate different questions. A Failure Mode describes a possible way a kind of thing could violate a requirement. A Failure Occurrence records an actual or suspected episode and can remain uncertain. A Failure Assessment examines occurrence, pattern, cause, impact, containment and recovery independently. Restoring the service does not resolve its cause. Keeping that uncertainty visible prevents a premature general lesson.
entries.editorial: Failure Mode describes a possible requirement violation. Failure Occurrence records an actual or suspected episode, including uncertainty. Failure Assessment separately examines occurrence, pattern, cause, impact, containment and recovery. Service restoration can leave cause unresolved. We should preserve that uncertainty before proposing a general lesson.

entries.original: An Incident coordinates response when related failures or uncertain impacts require an owner, timeline and resolution. A Failure Control Binding associates a specific failure-pattern version with a measure having one primary role: prevent, detect, contain, recover or compensate. It records intended treatment. Installation, execution and effectiveness need their own evidence. Incident closure retains history, uncertainties and follow-up obligations.
entries.editorial: An Incident organizes response when related failures or uncertain impacts need an owner, timeline and resolution. Failure Control Binding associates an exact pattern version with a measure having one primary role: prevention, detection, containment, recovery or compensation. The intended treatment leaves installation, execution and effectiveness to their own evidence. Closure preserves history, uncertainty and follow-up.

entries.original: Classification organizes these records using declared categories. A Classification Scheme defines separate questions, called axes, and permitted answers. A Classification Assignment records values for a particular thing and revision. The Classification Orthogonality Invariant requires each axis to serve a distinct decision or checking purpose, with dependencies stated explicitly. An impact label cannot also establish cause, recovery or permission. This lets agents retrieve relevant records without treating labels as conclusions.
entries.editorial: Classification supplies declared categories for finding relevant records. A Classification Scheme defines axes and permitted values; an Assignment binds values to a subject and revision. The Classification Orthogonality Invariant requires distinct decision or checking purposes, with dependencies explicit. An impact label supplies no conclusion about cause, recovery or permission.

entries.original: Feedback Record preserves an identifiable response such as a correction or rejection. Communication Preference records preferences about presentation, language or detail under stated conditions; Preference Application Assessment examines whether a particular preference applies to an output. A convenient review format does not broaden permission. Improvement Signals identify possible weaknesses or opportunities; owner-reviewed Improvement Targets route proposed work while retaining evidence and responsibility.
entries.editorial: Feedback Record preserves an attributable correction, rejection or other response. Communication Preference records presentation, language or detail under conditions; Preference Application Assessment checks applicability to an output. A preferred review format leaves permission unchanged. Improvement Signals identify possible opportunities, while owner-reviewed Improvement Targets route proposed work with evidence and responsibility.

entries.original: Park and colleagues studied stored observations, retrieved context, reflection and planning in a simulated community, reporting contributions to believable behavior. This supplies an architectural precedent within that study’s scope. It does not establish that a Lab lesson improves exports or that the study implements the Lab’s temporary-session contract. Generative Agents .
entries.editorial: Park and colleagues studied observations, retrieval, reflection and planning in a simulated community, reporting contributions to believable behavior. The study provides an architectural precedent within its scope. It proves neither export improvement from a Lab lesson nor implementation of the Lab’s temporary-session contract.

entries.original: The project retains observations, lesson versions, applications and assessments as saved records. Later agents obtain them through current Context and Ontology Views: task information and a selected connected model with source versions identified. These can inform future work. Changing a policy, software, agent profile or trained model weights is a separate governed change. The learning cycle does not grant automatic permission to modify itself.
entries.editorial: Observations, lesson versions, applications and assessments persist as project records. Later agents obtain them through current Context and Ontology Views with source versions identified. Those records can inform work. Changing policy, software, a profile or trained weights is a separate governed change, rather than an automatic learning-cycle permission.

entries.original: The export failure can therefore yield an inspectable account, advice for stated conditions, evidence of later use and a reviewed improvement. For the next agent, that account becomes usable input rather than private recollection. The project learns through records that can be challenged, revised and compared with later outcomes.
entries.editorial: The failure can leave an inspectable account, conditional advice, evidence of later use and a reviewed improvement. A future agent receives those records as task inputs. Others can challenge them, revise them and compare them with later outcomes.

entries.original: CyberAlchemy Lab is a framework for organizing project knowledge and work through definitions, record requirements, evidence and decisions. Understanding its current state requires distinguishing the model, accepted contracts, implemented software and observed executions. This essay uses the source snapshot inspected on 8 October 2026. It contains accepted Project State—the project’s saved records and knowledge—including acceptance of a local runtime implementation. Further product and release work remains.
entries.editorial: To understand the Lab’s current state, we need to distinguish the model, accepted contracts, implementation and observed executions. This essay retains the snapshot inspected on 8 October 2026. It includes accepted Project State and acceptance of a local runtime. Product and release work is still ahead.

entries.original: The snapshot selects 183 definition identities from 189 accepted versions. It selects 121 record-type contract bindings from 143 accepted contract records, alongside 41 connection-rule kinds. A binding identifies which contract applies to a record kind or selected schema section. There are 109 named endpoint kinds—the kinds of things that may occupy either end of a connection—and 550 permitted source–target kind pairs across the rules. These count different catalog entries, not installed features or complete graph coverage of project files.
entries.editorial: The snapshot selects 183 definition identities from 189 accepted versions, and 121 record-type contract bindings from 143 accepted contract records. It also selects 41 relation kinds, 109 endpoint kinds and 550 permitted ordered pairs. Bindings identify applicable contracts or schema sections. These totals count catalog entries, without measuring installed features or coverage of project files.

entries.original: The type registry also has descriptors, which are records describing available types and their status. It reports 114 selected accepted descriptors. Seven additional current bindings select sections inside a shared foundation schema, bringing the contract-binding count to 121. Separately, it retains seven unaccepted descriptors concerning earlier contracts, plus historical and duplicate-resolution records. The two sets of seven are different. This is why a catalog total is not a readiness score.
entries.editorial: The descriptor count is different: 114 selected accepted descriptors, plus seven bindings selecting shared foundation-schema sections, yield 121 bindings. Separately, seven unaccepted descriptors concern earlier contracts. Historical and duplicate-resolution records are retained too. The two sets of seven answer different questions, so the total is not a readiness score.

entries.original: A sequence of approvals established the operational foundation, initial Project State, an example of agent-context preparation and governance-transaction contracts. On 7 October 2026, another approval accepted the local runtime and its specified consequences. Its bundle contains 17 generated records, including updated Project State and six typed connections. Change and approval histories identify the same transition. A current-state reference locates that saved bundle; reconstruction still uses the history rather than treating the reference as a second source.
entries.editorial: Earlier approvals established the operational foundation, initial Project State, agent-context example and transaction contracts. On 7 October 2026, another approval accepted the local runtime and specified consequences. Its bundle has 17 generated records, including updated Project State and six typed connections. Both histories identify the transition. The current-state reference locates the bundle while history supplies reconstruction.

entries.original: The accepted implementation offers local commands on demand. They inspect catalogs, query authority, origins and lifecycle, prepare task information, apply locally authorized record changes, reconstruct state from history and recover within a tested scope. Formal acceptance is called admission. This admission excludes a general evaluator of organizational permissions, a continuously running service, external deployment and production durability. It records no runtime activation or external effect as part of that acceptance.
entries.editorial: The admitted implementation offers local commands on demand for inspection, governance queries, task preparation, authorized record changes, reconstruction and bounded recovery. Its admission excludes a general organizational-permission evaluator, continuous service, external deployment and production durability. That acceptance records no activation or external effect.

entries.original: The software uses a fixed earlier selection of definitions, state and history records. Later accepted changes do not automatically update that selection. A proposed successor selects the later state while retaining the earlier implementation. Its review contains a validation record reporting 38 passing checks and an isolated work-and-context demonstration. Those recorded results support the proposal; the update still requires separate acceptance. This writing task did not rerun those checks.
entries.editorial: The runtime uses a fixed earlier source selection. Later acceptance does not update it automatically. A proposed successor selects later state while retaining the earlier implementation. Its review records 38 passing checks and an isolated work-and-context demonstration. Those results support the proposal, whose acceptance is still separate. This editorial pass reruns none of those implementation checks.

entries.original: A returning agent needs to know which accepted state its prepared information represents and whether newer records exist. The fixed source selection makes that boundary important. The proposed update addresses selection of the later state. Keeping software selections and task information aligned with accepted changes is further work in the repeatable-operation roadmap stage.
entries.editorial: A returning agent needs the accepted-state identity behind its context and an account of newer records. The fixed selection makes that boundary visible. The proposed update addresses later-state selection. Keeping runtime selections and task information aligned remains part of repeatable-operation work.

entries.original: Ontology work has its own evidence. An ontology is a structured model of concepts, things and relationships. The integration records include acceptance of an implementation binding, adoption of a particular Rust lifecycle library and an authorized past local command execution. A migration prototype has a bounded product approval. Its manifest lists 21 packages, 815 graph nodes, 1,210 relationships and 422 supporting documents. Imported records retain their source qualifications; importing them does not accept every source meaning or establish coverage of all current project objects.
entries.editorial: Ontology evidence has its own scope. The records include acceptance of an implementation binding, adoption of a Rust lifecycle library and an authorized past local execution. A migration prototype has bounded product approval. Its manifest lists 21 packages, 815 nodes, 1,210 relationships and 422 documents. Imports retain source qualifications and supply no blanket acceptance or coverage of current objects.

entries.original: The lifecycle library can load events, reconstruct consistent recorded states, join matching governance records and generate selected information views. Those graphs are calculated outputs. Some implementation overviews retain proposed-status wording from earlier work; later acceptance and adoption records establish their effective status. Adoption does not establish a currently running service. Past execution, current operation and the switch of consumers to a new implementation are separate claims.
entries.editorial: The lifecycle library loads events, reconstructs consistent cuts, joins governance records and produces views. The graphs are calculated outputs. Some overviews retain earlier proposed wording; subsequent acceptance and adoption establish effective standing. Adoption, past execution, current operation and consumer cutover need separate evidence.

entries.original: The proposed roadmap groups further work into stages. Foundation records controlled local operation. Repeatable operation adds continuity across accepted changes and refreshed agent information. Integrated work connects engineering, research, failure assessment and later lesson use. A coherent ontology covers an explicitly selected migration scope. A usable product adds installation, recovery, upgrades and stable-release criteria. Their presence in a plan does not establish that these outcomes have been achieved.
entries.editorial: The roadmap proposes foundation, repeatable operation, integrated work, a scoped coherent ontology and a usable product. These add continuity, refreshed agent information, engineering and research connections, failure assessment, lesson use, installation, recovery and upgrades. Planning the stages leaves their completion to evidence.

entries.original: The intended working loop connects these pieces. Record a need, select a response, prepare current information and permissions, perform the assigned work and assess results. A responsible owner reviews proposed changes to saved records. Authorized consequences enter Project State and its separate change and approval histories. Updated views prepare the next agent session. Failures and feedback can also produce lessons whose later use and benefit are assessed.
entries.editorial: The intended loop starts with a need and response, then current information and permission for assigned work. Results are assessed, owners review proposed changes, and authorized consequences enter Project State with separate change and approval histories. Updated views prepare the next session. Failures and feedback can also produce lessons whose use and benefit are assessed.

entries.original: A useful next demonstration would take one real Work item through that loop under an authorized runtime selection, accept another change, then prepare a new session. It should show continuity across the change, recovery and treatment of evidence or unresolved work. The repeatable-operation stage proposes that demonstration. Permanent provisioning and activation require their own operational authorization.
entries.editorial: A useful next demonstration would take a real Work item through that loop under an authorized runtime selection, accept another change and prepare a fresh session. It should show continuity, recovery and handling of evidence or unresolved work. The repeatable-operation stage proposes it. Permanent provisioning and activation still need operational authorization.

entries.original: A stable product release remains unestablished. Its prerequisites include product architecture, source-authority selection rules, publication review, repeatable evidence and an owner’s approval of the exact release. The Lab therefore has an accepted local foundation alongside unfinished work. Its purpose is to let later participants recover that state and its limits from explicit records, then contribute results another session can examine.
entries.editorial: A stable release has yet to be established. Architecture, source-authority rules, publication review, repeatable evidence and approval of exact release bytes are prerequisites. The Lab has an accepted local foundation with unfinished work alongside it. Explicit records let the next participant recover those facts and contribute results another session can examine.

entries.original: We're building Craft, a system for software design, domain modeling and enforceable architecture, as we prepare for a closed beta. Our goal is to compile software from an explicit model, preserving its meaning through the choices that shape the code.
entries.editorial: We’re building Craft as a software-design, domain-modeling and enforceable-architecture product for a closed beta. The aim is to compile software from an explicit model, keeping its meaning connected to the choices that shape the code.

entries.original: Craft is the software-design product in CyberAlchemy Lab's broader model of knowledge and work. The Lab guide explains how a requirement becomes a project, assigned work and evidence for an owner decision. This article follows the software model and implementation that can be developed within that work. Craft has its own design contracts; using its tools does not by itself accept a Lab record or authorize deployment.
entries.editorial: Craft sits within CyberAlchemy Lab’s wider model of knowledge and work. The Lab guide follows a requirement into a project, assigned work and evidence for an owner decision. Here we follow the software model and implementation developed during that work. Craft’s design contracts and the Lab’s acceptance and deployment decisions retain their own responsibilities.

entries.original: Domain-Driven Design provides a useful starting point: develop a model with people who understand the domain, build a shared language around it, and keep that model connected to the implementation. Its language has a defined context, so the same word can carry different meanings in different parts of a business. Eric Evans, Domain-Driven Design Reference
entries.editorial: Domain-Driven Design gives us a starting point: build a model with people who understand the domain, develop a shared language and keep the implementation connected to it. That language has a context. The same word can mean different things in different parts of a business.

entries.original: A software model makes the system's meanings and responsibilities explicit: which concepts exist, what behavior they have, which states matter and how responsibilities connect. For example, it can distinguish deciding whether a request is acceptable from changing state to fulfill that request. Those responsibilities can use the same information while having different consequences.
entries.editorial: A software model states the concepts, behavior, states and connections a design depends on. Consider deciding whether a request is acceptable and changing state to fulfill it. Those jobs might use the same information, yet they have different consequences. The model gives us a way to name and examine both.

entries.original: This gives implementation a reference to work from. A developer can examine what a concept means, which responsibility belongs to it and which interactions the design permits. The same reference helps a later contributor understand what a change must preserve.
entries.editorial: A developer can return to the model to understand a concept’s meaning, its responsibility and permitted interactions. The same reference helps someone joining later work understand what a change needs to preserve.

entries.original: Shopify's account of modularizing its monolith makes the architectural problem concrete. Shipping and checkout code had become tightly coupled. Organizing components was followed by work to isolate dependencies, define public interfaces and track access that crossed domain boundaries. The problem involved deciding which interactions were allowed and observing whether the code respected those decisions. Shopify engineering, 2019
entries.editorial: Shopify’s monolith example makes the architectural issue concrete. Shipping and checkout had become tightly coupled. The team worked on dependency isolation, public interfaces and visibility into access across domain boundaries. Organizing components was part of deciding which interactions were allowed and observing whether the implementation followed those decisions.

entries.original: The model of behavior can be equally important. Stripe's PaymentIntent lifecycle distinguishes a payment requiring customer action, one still processing and one that has succeeded. Asynchronous payment methods can take days to resolve. For a service deciding when to fulfill an order, these distinctions change what “complete” means and when the next action is permitted. Stripe's payment lifecycle documentation
entries.editorial: Behavior needs similar care. Stripe’s PaymentIntent distinguishes customer action, processing and success. Some asynchronous methods take days. For fulfillment, those states affect what “complete” means and when the next action is permitted.

entries.original: Together, these examples connect meaning to architecture: a payment's state determines when fulfillment may begin, while the boundaries between components determine where that responsibility belongs. Implementation needs to preserve both. The difficulty is carrying those decisions through changes to the software and the people or agents working on it.
entries.editorial: In these examples, meaning and architecture meet in an action: a payment state governs when fulfillment begins, and component boundaries govern where the responsibility belongs. Both need to survive software changes and handoffs to new people or agents.

entries.original: Those decisions often remain distributed across discussions, diagrams, prose and existing code. People may agree on where a business rule belongs, which information an operation can read and what should happen when it fails, without recording those obligations precisely enough for a later contributor to recover them.
entries.editorial: Those decisions often live across conversation, diagrams, prose and code. A team might agree where a rule belongs or what should happen after failure without leaving a precise account for the next contributor. That becomes a problem when someone has to recover the design.

entries.original: The difficulty appears when an assumption is preserved in conversation but lost during implementation, or when code changes an obligation without making that change explicit. An order is fulfilled too early. A retry repeats an effect. A change in one component breaks behavior elsewhere.
entries.editorial: An assumption can survive in conversation and disappear from implementation. Code can also change an obligation without recording that change. An order gets fulfilled too early, a retry repeats an effect, or one component’s change breaks another. The visible symptom is only part of the story.

entries.original: The visible failure may be a wrong result or a failing test. Understanding it requires tracing the assumptions, responsibilities and dependencies behind that symptom. The code may still contain familiar names even though the conditions those names once represented have changed.
entries.editorial: A wrong result or failing check gives us a starting point. Understanding it means following the assumptions, responsibilities and dependencies behind the symptom. Familiar names can remain in the code while the conditions they once represented have changed.

entries.original: Agentic engineering adds another source of discontinuity. Work can span several sessions, each with only part of the design context. Anthropic's work on long-running coding agents describes unfinished work with unclear handoffs, later sessions guessing what happened, and completion claims made without sufficient end-to-end testing. Anthropic, Effective harnesses for long-running agents
entries.editorial: Agent work introduces more handoffs. A task can span sessions with partial design context. Anthropic’s work on long-running coding agents describes unclear unfinished work, later sessions guessing at earlier progress and completion claims lacking enough end-to-end evaluation. That gives us a concrete continuity problem to examine.

entries.original: An agent can also understand the requirement and still leave the work incomplete. It may implement the main path but omit a failure branch, define a rule without connecting it to the operation, or update one component while leaving a dependent caller unchanged. Mentioning a required action in the task does not ensure that it reaches the finished result. The code that exists may look coherent; the missing piece becomes visible only when someone compares the result with the full requirement or exercises the neglected path.
entries.editorial:
An agent can understand a requirement and still omit part of the work. It might implement the main path, leave a failure branch out, declare a rule without using it, or update a component while leaving a caller unchanged.

The omission becomes visible when someone compares the result with the whole requirement or exercises the missing path. Listing an action in a task does not ensure its completion.

entries.original: This creates a practical review problem: inspecting the patch tells us what changed, but identifying what was never implemented requires a separate account of what should have been delivered. Completion needs to be assessed against explicit obligations, including required connections, branches and follow-up actions.
entries.editorial: A patch shows what changed. To find what was never delivered, we need an account of the required work too. Connections, branches and follow-up actions belong in that completion assessment.

entries.original: An agent might weaken an acceptance condition to make a failing request succeed, duplicate a business rule in a convenient component, or update a test to match changed behavior without examining the requirement. The patch can look reasonable in isolation while changing the conditions the system was meant to preserve.
entries.editorial: A plausible patch might weaken a condition to make a request succeed, copy a rule into a convenient component, or change a test without examining the requirement. Looking at the patch alone can miss a change to the meaning the system was supposed to preserve.

entries.original: The review needs to distinguish repairing the implementation from revising the requirement. Otherwise, an attempt to fix a symptom can silently change the system's meaning.
entries.editorial: The reviewer needs to know whether the proposal repairs implementation or revises the requirement. That question matters before a symptom fix becomes a different business rule.

entries.original: Another failure mode is brittleness through accumulated design shortcuts . An agent may choose the first convenient way to satisfy the immediate request: add a condition to an existing function, copy a rule into a new caller or reach directly into another component's data. The change can work for today's case while leaving responsibilities more entangled. Later work inherits those choices and adds further exceptions around them.
entries.editorial: Shortcuts can accumulate. An agent adds a condition, copies a rule into a caller or reaches into another component’s data because it solves the immediate example. The next change inherits that structure, and another exception makes the responsibilities harder to recover.

entries.original: This creates technical debt: future changes require more coordination, investigation and repair because earlier design decisions made the structure harder to change. A capacity rule copied into several callers must be updated in several places. A function combining decision, persistence and retry behavior becomes difficult to modify without affecting all three.
entries.editorial: That leaves future work with more coordination and repair. A copied capacity rule needs several updates. A function combining decisions, persistence and retry behavior makes a change to one responsibility affect the others. Those are concrete forms of technical debt.

entries.original: The important design question is whether the responsibilities remain clear as the software grows. A small implementation can support later changes when its boundaries are explicit. When new behavior repeatedly arrives as another exception or copy, a routine feature can require extensive reconstruction of the system, and repeated regressions can make further development impractical without redesign.
entries.editorial: The design question is how responsibilities hold up as the software grows. Explicit boundaries help a small implementation accommodate later changes. Repeated exceptions and copies can make a routine feature require reconstruction, with regressions eventually forcing redesign.

entries.original: Research now examines this across successive changes. SlopCodeBench lets agents repeatedly extend their own code under evolving specifications and reports increasing redundant code and concentrated complexity in many evaluated trajectories. CodeTaste finds that agents are better at implementing detailed refactoring instructions than identifying the refactorings human developers chose. These results support examining how a design evolves across changes, alongside whether the current change works. SlopCodeBench, May 2026 preprint ; CodeTaste, ICML 2026 .
entries.editorial: Research examines successive changes too. SlopCodeBench reports growing redundancy and concentrated complexity in many evaluated trajectories. CodeTaste finds agents more successful with detailed refactoring instructions than with identifying human-selected refactorings. These results support examining the sequence of changes alongside the current result.

entries.original: These failures leave the next contributor with several kinds of reconstruction: recover the intended meaning, identify missing work and discover which responsibilities moved or became entangled. Addressing them requires a model that distinguishes those responsibilities and records what each one must preserve. Craft's taxonomy provides the vocabulary for doing that.
entries.editorial: The next contributor has to recover meaning, find missing work and understand responsibilities that moved or became entangled. Craft’s taxonomy gives us vocabulary for distinguishing those jobs and stating what each must preserve.

entries.original: A taxonomy classifies concepts by their responsibilities. Craft's categories answer practical design questions: what has an identity, what computes a value, what governs a decision, what changes state and what coordinates several actions?
entries.editorial: A taxonomy helps answer practical questions. What has identity? Which responsibility derives a value, decides a condition, changes state or coordinates actions? Craft’s categories give those answers names.

entries.original: Each category establishes the kind of contract a concept needs. A Rule requires a condition with a boolean result; a Workflow requires an account of the Operations it coordinates. The project then supplies the specific condition or coordination being designed.
entries.editorial: The category tells us which contract the concept needs. A Rule needs a Boolean condition, while a Workflow needs an account of coordinated Operations. The project then supplies the particular condition or coordination being designed.

entries.original: The word “type” appears at two levels here.
