A meta-type identifies a concept's responsibility; a field's value type, such as a string or unsigned integer, identifies the information that field can hold. Naming a concept Entity establishes an identity obligation. Declaring one of its fields as a string constrains that field's values. A typed model makes both kinds of declaration explicit.
entries.editorial: “Type” refers to two things here. A meta-type names responsibility; a value type such as string or unsigned integer constrains a field’s contents. Declaring Entity creates an identity obligation. Declaring a string field restricts its values. A typed model makes both choices explicit.

entries.original: The graph's nodes represent project concepts and their contracts. Runtime objects are instances of those concepts. A single Entity node can describe a type with many objects in a running system; adding another object does not require adding another type to the model.
entries.editorial: The graph records concepts and contracts. Runtime objects instantiate those concepts. One Entity node can describe many running objects, so another object does not require another type node.

entries.original: Craft groups its 13 active backend meta-types into four families: structural, behavioral, connective and lifecycle. A project selects the roles its design needs. It does not have to instantiate every category.
entries.editorial: Craft’s 13 active backend meta-types fall into structural, behavioral, connective and lifecycle families. A project selects the responsibilities its design needs. The catalog supplies choices, without requiring every category in every model.

entries.original: The distinction between Entity and Value Object determines how sameness is understood. An Entity can retain its identity while its fields change. Two Value Objects with equal contents represent the same value under their declared equality rule. This affects references, updates and comparisons.
entries.editorial: Identity changes how we understand sameness. An Entity keeps its identity while fields change. Value Objects with equal contents have the same value under their declared equality rule. References, updates and comparisons need that distinction.

entries.original: An Enum defines which alternatives exist. It does not say which transitions between alternatives are permitted. That second responsibility belongs to a State Machine.
entries.editorial: An Enum declares alternatives. To decide which transitions between them are permitted, we need a State Machine. The list of alternatives alone leaves that behavior unspecified.

entries.original: A Query reads domain information. A Calculation derives a value from the inputs it receives; it has no Entity-reading relationship in the current catalog. This keeps retrieval and computation identifiable even when both return data. A Query's result can change when the underlying information changes; read-only behavior does not imply permanently identical answers.
entries.editorial: A Query retrieves domain information. A Calculation derives a value from supplied inputs and has no Entity-reading relationship in the current catalog. Both can return data while owning different jobs. A read-only Query can return a different result when its underlying information changes.

entries.original: A Rule returns true or false for its declared condition. A Policy selects how behavior proceeds. Keeping those results distinct lets a reviewer identify whether a proposed change alters eligibility or changes the strategy used after a choice is permitted.
entries.editorial: A Rule returns true or false for a condition. A Policy selects how behavior proceeds. Reviewing a change means asking whether eligibility changed or a strategy changed after an allowed choice.

entries.original: An Operation's contract declares its state boundary. Reads identify information it uses; writes identify state it changes; external effects identify interactions beyond that state boundary. A guard references the Rule whose predicate , or true-or-false condition, governs the action. The contract must also state what happens if that condition fails. A rejected attempt can leave state unchanged while the successful action owns the declared change. A pure function classifying supplied values belongs to Calculation, as the capacity example demonstrates below.
entries.editorial: An Operation declares its state boundary through reads, writes and external effects. Its guard refers to the Rule governing the action, and the contract needs failure behavior too. A rejection can leave state unchanged while a successful action owns the change. A pure classifier of supplied values belongs to Calculation.

entries.original: A Workflow owns coordination across Operations. Each Operation retains responsibility for its own changes and effects. When recovery is required, the design also needs to distinguish deciding that recovery is necessary from actually executing a compensating action. The current taxonomy incorporates the role formerly called Saga into Workflow.
entries.editorial: Workflow coordinates Operations, each of which keeps responsibility for its changes and effects. Recovery adds another distinction: evaluating the need for recovery and executing compensation have separate jobs. The current taxonomy places the earlier Saga role within Workflow.

entries.original: An Interface defines what a consumer may call. A Mapping defines how information changes shape when crossing a boundary. Those responsibilities can work together while remaining independently inspectable.
entries.editorial: An Interface declares calls available to a consumer. A Mapping changes information’s shape across a boundary. They can cooperate without becoming the same responsibility.

entries.original: An Event expresses a past occurrence. A request to perform work belongs to a different part of the design. Confusing the two makes it unclear whether a consumer is being asked to act or being informed that an action has already happened.
entries.editorial: An Event records a past occurrence. A request asks for work. The distinction tells a consumer whether something has happened or whether someone is asking it to act.

entries.original: The Interface role also has a specific domain meaning. A language-level interface for a repository, clock or transaction provider can serve an implementation concern without becoming a domain Interface node. Such infrastructure contracts support the model's implementation and need their own declared boundaries.
entries.editorial: The domain Interface role has a narrower meaning than every interface in source code. A repository, clock or transaction-provider interface can serve implementation infrastructure without becoming a domain Interface node. Those infrastructure boundaries still need explicit contracts.

entries.original: This adds obligations that a list of state names cannot express: which event permits a transition, which condition must hold, what effect follows and which invariants remain true. The lifecycle can then be examined as behavior over time.
entries.editorial: A lifecycle adds behavior beyond a list of state names: triggering events, required conditions, effects and preserved invariants. We can then examine what happens over time.

entries.original: A relationship has a source, a verb and a target. Its signature declares which roles are permitted at the two ends. Its scope declares where the connection may be used. A feature is an ownership and organization unit in the model; a connection within one feature and a connection across features can carry different obligations.
entries.editorial: A relationship names a source, verb and target. Its signature permits particular roles at the ends, and its scope limits where the connection applies. Feature ownership makes an internal connection and a cross-feature connection carry different obligations.

entries.original: These distinctions describe different responsibilities. Produces identifies the action causing an Event; emits identifies its Entity subject or source. Owns declares a responsibility boundary; belongs-to declares membership or assignment and does not establish ownership. Reads records a dependency without implying that every other part of the reading Operation is free of writes.
entries.editorial: The verbs answer different questions. produces links the action causing an Event; emits identifies its Entity subject or source. owns establishes a responsibility boundary. belongs-to records membership or assignment without proving ownership. reads records a dependency while leaving other Operation writes to their own declarations.

entries.original: Multiplicity also matters. In the current creates relationship, one Operation concept can be the creation owner of at most one Entity type, and that Entity type can have at most one such owner. The Operation can still create many instances at runtime. This is a constraint on the design's ownership structure, not a limit on how many objects may exist.
entries.editorial: The creates signature also constrains multiplicity. One Operation concept owns creation of at most one Entity type, and that type has at most one such creation owner. The Operation can still create many runtime instances. The limit concerns design ownership.

entries.original: Typed references inside a contract remain distinct from graph relationships. An input can refer to an Entity type, and a result can refer to an Enum, without introducing new relationship verbs. Similarly, a field declaration supplies information that need not become a separate graph edge. A new verb needs a distinct meaning and an explicit extension to the catalog, including endpoint, scope and composition rules.
entries.editorial: Typed contract references are separate from graph relationships. An input can name an Entity type, a result can name an Enum, and a field can describe data without introducing a new edge. A new verb needs a distinct meaning and explicit endpoint, scope and composition rules in the catalog.

entries.original: The architecture profile can further constrain a connection that the catalog permits. A valid signature is therefore one part of deciding whether a particular composition is allowed.
entries.editorial: A permitted catalog signature is only part of a composition decision. The selected architecture profile can restrict the connection further. We need both before calling the composition allowed.

entries.original: The model also has a proposed vocabulary for user interfaces. These roles describe navigation, presentation, input and access to backend responsibilities. Their status differs from the active backend core: nine are candidates, and two further labels remain deferred while their boundaries are resolved.
entries.editorial: The UI vocabulary addresses navigation, presentation, input and backend access. Nine roles are candidates and two labels are deferred while boundaries are resolved. That standing differs from the active backend core.

entries.original: A View Model shapes presentation without acquiring authority to redefine the domain. A UI Guard applies a source Rule; showing or hiding a Page does not independently authorize a backend action. Likewise, a Component is a specific visual responsibility: more specific responsibilities such as routing and form validation retain their own roles.
entries.editorial: A View Model shapes presentation while leaving domain meaning to its governing source. A UI Guard applies a Rule; hiding or showing a Page supplies no backend authorization. Components have visual responsibilities, with routing and form validation retaining their more specific roles.

entries.original: Two names need care. A UI Guard is a proposed node role; an Operation's guard is a reference to the Rule governing that action. A UI Binding records endpoint use; an artifact's binding records its connection to the model and implementation selections that produced it. Each term needs its context to remain explicit.
entries.editorial: Two overloaded names deserve attention. UI Guard is a proposed node role; an Operation guard refers to its Rule. UI Binding records endpoint use; artifact binding traces model and implementation inputs. The context tells us which meaning applies.

entries.original: These signatures describe the intended connections without making every participating role an active backend type. In particular, the catalog retains connections involving the deferred Adapter and State Indicator roles. Their presence does not settle those roles' open boundaries or establish a complete compiled UI implementation. The UI and UI-to-backend signatures are scoped within a feature; crossing layers does not automatically permit crossing feature ownership boundaries.
entries.editorial: The intended signatures include deferred Adapter and State Indicator roles. Their presence settles neither the open role boundaries nor compiled UI completeness. UI and UI-to-backend connections are within-feature signatures. Crossing a layer supplies no automatic permission to cross feature ownership.

entries.original: The taxonomy identifies the responsibilities available to a design. Architecture profiles and realizations then specify how a selected design is organized and represented in code. A role can have different supported implementation forms while retaining the same responsibility and contract.
entries.editorial: Taxonomy gives us responsibilities. Architecture profiles and realizations choose organization and code representation. Different supported forms can implement the same responsibility, provided its contract stays intact.

entries.original: Manifests, build receipts, observations and evidence records describe construction and examination of the software. They serve the work around the model; they are not additional backend meta-types. A Craft receipt records a particular construction or check. Retaining it in Lab Project State requires the applicable recording contract, attribution and permission; its existence does not supply an admission decision. Project State and agent handoffs preserve knowledge about the design and work performed without becoming the domain behavior being compiled.
entries.editorial: Manifests, receipts, observations and evidence describe construction and examination around the model. They add no backend meta-types. A Craft receipt records a particular construction or check; saving it in Lab Project State needs the applicable recording contract, attribution and permission. It supplies no admission decision. Handoff knowledge is separate from compiled domain behavior.

entries.original: Craft uses explicit model declarations as compiler input. The selected model, architecture profile and realizations become the reference for construction and later inspection. The active role vocabulary describes what can be modeled; code construction depends on the exact contracts and realizations supported by the selected compiler. An active role does not establish uniform compiler support for every behavior or language.
entries.editorial: Compilation starts from explicit declarations and selected profiles and realizations. The active vocabulary describes modelable responsibilities. Actual code generation depends on the exact contracts and forms the selected compiler supports. Active standing alone establishes no uniform language or behavior support.

entries.original: Before construction, contributors must also review the choices the compiler will receive. Adding persistence introduces a state owner and failure behavior. Adding an entry point introduces a consumer. Adding a retry introduces questions about repeated effects. The model gives these design changes an explicit subject to examine before they become code.
entries.editorial: Before construction, we need to review those choices. Persistence adds state ownership and failure behavior. An entry point adds a consumer. A retry raises repeated-effect questions. The model gives each change a subject to examine before code exists.

entries.original: Each question needs its own review or evidence. A valid model can still omit a business requirement, and conforming code can still await integration or evaluation.
entries.editorial: Each question needs review or evidence. A structurally valid model might omit a business requirement, and conforming code might still await integration or evaluation. We need to keep those open questions visible.

entries.original: AI can help explore the domain, author the model and investigate disagreements. Producing the supported source code follows the compiler's explicit translation rules, so each coding session need not reconstruct and handwrite the same declared behavior.
entries.editorial: AI can help explore the domain, author declarations and investigate disagreements. Supported source-code construction follows explicit compiler translations. The next session can use those declarations instead of reconstructing and handwriting the same behavior.

entries.original: We can now follow that process through a capacity decision for a compute service. The example uses four backend roles—Entity, Rule, Calculation and Enum—with explicit typed references. Starting with a narrow decision makes each obligation visible; later sections add reservation and retries to show how the same design can evolve.
entries.editorial: Let’s follow a compute-service capacity decision. Entity, Rule, Calculation and Enum supply four backend roles with typed references. Starting with this narrow decision makes its obligations visible. Reservation and retry work will add further responsibilities later.

entries.original: Consider an agent asked to implement a capacity decision for a compute service. A caller supplies a request identifier, the number of units requested and the number available. The business wants some capacity to remain after a request of that size. The decision must reject requests that would consume all available capacity, and it must leave state unchanged.
entries.editorial: A caller supplies a request identity, requested units and available units. The business wants capacity left after a request of that size. The decision must reject a request consuming all available capacity and leave state unchanged. Those conditions belong in the model before implementation.

entries.original: For example, request R-104 asks for 4 units when 5 are available. It should be accepted. A request for all 5 should be rejected.
entries.editorial: R-104 requests 4 units from 5 available, so acceptance is expected. A request for all 5 should be rejected. The boundary is part of the requirement.

entries.original: “Accept when capacity is sufficient” does not fully express that requirement: it leaves the equality boundary open. Before implementing it, the agent and reviewer need a precise account of what acceptance means.
entries.editorial: “Accept when capacity is sufficient” leaves equality unresolved. The agent and reviewer need to decide precisely what acceptance means before writing its implementation.

entries.original: A snapshot is the supplied record of the request and capacity quantities used for this decision. Acceptance means that the request satisfies the condition in that record. It does not mean that capacity has been reserved or a job has started.
entries.editorial: The snapshot supplies the request and capacity quantities for this decision. Accept means the condition holds for that record. Reservation and job execution are still separate responsibilities.

entries.original: Once accepted for this scope, the definition gives the agent and reviewer a durable reference: preserve the strict boundary and keep the decision separate from reservation. A proposal to allow equality revises the meaning of acceptance. A proposal to reserve capacity adds a responsibility with state ownership and consistency rules. Both require a design change, and the selected definition makes the difference visible.
entries.editorial: Once accepted within scope, the definition gives later work a stable reference for the strict boundary and separation from reservation. Allowing equality revises acceptance’s meaning. Reserving capacity adds state ownership and consistency requirements. Both need explicit design changes.

entries.original: The definition fixes the condition. The model must identify the information it uses, the responsibility that derives a decision and the complete set of results. Those requirements give us four concepts:
entries.editorial: The condition is now stated. We still need to identify the supplied information, the responsibility deriving a decision and the allowed results. Four concepts give those obligations a place in the model.

entries.original: The snapshot declares a request identifier and two unsigned integer quantities—whole numbers that cannot be negative. In request R-104 , these quantities are 4 requested units and 5 available units. The model explicitly marks the request identifier as its identity.
entries.editorial: The snapshot has a request identifier and two unsigned integer quantities, whole numbers that cannot be negative. R-104 uses 4 requested units and 5 available. The identifier is explicitly selected as the record’s identity.

entries.original: Classify capacity takes a supplied snapshot and returns a Capacity decision. Its conditional expression calls the existing Within capacity Rule, returning Accept when the Rule is true and Reject otherwise. It owns no retrieval, mutation or external effect. The Rule remains the single declared source of the strict comparison.
entries.editorial: Classify capacity accepts the supplied snapshot and returns a Capacity decision. Its conditional expression calls Within capacity, producing Accept when true and Reject otherwise. Retrieval, mutation and external effects are absent from this responsibility. The Rule supplies the single declared strict comparison.

entries.original: The earlier compiler fixture labeled this pure decision as an Operation. The corrected example uses Calculation and preserves Operation's state-changing meaning. The earlier fixture is retained as historical compiler evidence; it no longer supplies the role guidance used in this article.
entries.editorial: The earlier fixture called the pure decision an Operation. The corrected example uses Calculation, preserving Operation’s state-changing meaning. The fixture stays as historical compiler evidence, with current role guidance supplied by this correction.

entries.original: This summary explains the model; the compiler consumes the corresponding structured contracts. The conditional Enum result uses domainspec.typed-calculation/v2 . Existing v1 Calculations retain their UInt64 arithmetic contract. The v2 contract supports one conditional expression with explicit scalar or named record inputs, a typed Rule expression and a payloadless Enum result. It does not introduce an Operation guard or write/effect declarations.
entries.editorial: The compiler consumes structured contracts behind this summary. domainspec.typed-calculation/v2 supports a conditional expression with explicit scalar or named-record inputs, a typed Rule expression and a payloadless Enum result. Numeric v1 Calculations keep their UInt64 arithmetic contract. The successor adds neither Operation guards nor write or effect declarations.

entries.original: Reject is a normal value in this classification. It is neither an exception nor evidence that execution failed. Both alternatives must be declared before code is constructed.
entries.editorial: Reject is an ordinary result of the classification. It says neither that execution failed nor that an exception occurred. The model needs both alternatives before construction.

entries.original: With 4 requested units and 5 available units, classification returns Accept and available capacity remains 5. A separate Reserve capacity Operation would check current capacity and coordinate that check with a state change: reduce available capacity from 5 to 1 and create a 4-unit reservation. A request of 5 units fails the strict condition and leaves capacity unchanged.
entries.editorial: Classifying 4 against 5 returns Accept and leaves available capacity at 5. A separate Reserve capacity Operation would check current state, reduce capacity to 1 and create a 4-unit reservation together. A request for 5 fails the strict condition and leaves capacity unchanged.

entries.original: The successful reservation owns a change; a rejected attempt can leave state unchanged. The supplied snapshot's Accept value is insufficient to reserve live capacity, because another request may have changed it. Reservation needs its own state owner, authorization and consistency contract. The current compiled example implements classification; reservation remains a design extension.
entries.editorial: The reservation owns the successful change. A rejected attempt can leave state unchanged. Meanwhile, another request might make a snapshot’s Accept stale for live reservation. Reservation therefore needs its own owner, authorization and consistency contract. The compiled example covers classification; reservation is an extension.

entries.original: The classifier names its snapshot input type, its decision result type and the Rule called by its expression. These references form a checked dependency closure: the exact declarations needed to construct this calculation.
entries.editorial: The classifier names its snapshot type, result type and called Rule. Together they form the checked dependency closure needed to construct this Calculation.

entries.original: These dependencies must resolve. The Rule reference must supply its exact parameters with compatible types. The result constructors must name variants in the selected Enum. The referenced properties must belong to the supplied record. A Rule sitting elsewhere in the project is insufficient unless the classifier actually binds it.
entries.editorial: Every dependency must resolve: required Rule parameters, compatible types, selected Enum variants and properties belonging to the supplied record. Merely placing the Rule elsewhere in the project leaves its use unbound.

entries.original: An expression reference and an authored software relationship have different contracts. The existing enforces signature connects Rule to Operation; reads connects Query or Operation to Entity. Neither signature admits this Calculation endpoint. Reclassifying the example therefore removes those edges from the current design rather than changing their permitted endpoints.
entries.editorial: Expression references and authored relationships have different contracts. enforces admits Rule to Operation, and reads admits Query or Operation to Entity. Neither admits this Calculation endpoint. Correcting the example removes those edges instead of broadening their signatures.

entries.original: If the design adds reservation, Within capacity can enforce the new Operation. A Calculation can calculate a derived value for that Operation when the Operation actually uses it. Those are already permitted signatures, and the state-changing design must declare its own connections. A new kind of connection would require a catalog extension.
entries.editorial: Reservation could use the existing Within capacity Rule through enforces. An actually used Calculation could derive a value for the Operation under an existing signature. The state-changing design must declare those connections. A new meaning would need a catalog extension.

entries.original: The decision remains self-contained: a caller provides a record and receives Accept or Reject. We then select an architecture profile and supported implementation forms that preserve this boundary. The profile constrains placement and dependencies within the wider application. A handwritten caller still needs examination: it could duplicate the comparison, ignore the decision or add an undeclared reservation.
entries.editorial: A caller supplies the record and receives Accept or Reject. An architecture profile and supported realizations should preserve that boundary while governing placement and dependencies. A handwritten caller still needs review for duplicated rules, ignored decisions or undeclared reservation.

entries.original: For this selection, the compiler constructs the snapshot record, decision alternatives, Rule and conditional Calculation. The resulting artifacts retain bindings to the model and implementation selections used to produce them. Later inspection can therefore identify which design each output is expected to implement.
entries.editorial: For this selection, the compiler constructs the snapshot, result alternatives, Rule and conditional Calculation. The outputs retain model and realization bindings. A later reviewer has an exact design to compare with each artifact.

entries.original: The Rule and its use are constructed together: the strict comparison becomes within_capacity , and the Calculation calls it before selecting Accept or Reject. This addresses the omission described earlier. Declaring the comparison alone is insufficient; the selected contracts also require its use and both outcomes. Their construction follows explicit translation rules, so the agent need not remember to handwrite each piece separately.
entries.editorial: The generated Rule implements within_capacity, and the Calculation calls it before choosing Accept or Reject. The selected contracts require that use and both outcomes. Explicit translations construct the connected behavior, reducing what the agent has to remember to assemble by hand.

entries.original: This gives the reviewer a trace from each declared obligation to its code. “The function exists” is a weaker claim than showing that it calls the selected Rule, covers both results and keeps the declared state boundary.
entries.editorial: The reviewer can trace declared obligations into code. Finding a function is a starting point. We also need its selected Rule call, both outcomes and preserved state boundary.

entries.original: For the same selected model and compilation inputs, the intended construction is deterministic. The resulting artifacts remain bound to the source and selections that produced them, giving later inspection a precise subject. That construction covers the selected supported contracts; it does not invent a caller, deployment procedure or business requirement absent from the model.
entries.editorial: Construction is intended to be deterministic for identical selected inputs. The artifacts bind to their source and selections, giving later inspection an exact subject. The supported contracts supply that construction; absent callers, deployment procedures or requirements remain absent.

entries.original: “Enforcement” needs a concrete subject. Model validation checks declarations and connections. Artifact inspection checks the selected output. The executable Rule condition determines the decision when the function runs, and behavioral evaluation examines that execution.
entries.editorial: “Enforcement” needs a subject. Model validation examines declarations, artifact inspection examines output, the executable Rule governs a running decision, and behavioral evaluation examines that execution. They support different claims.

entries.original: For the capacity example, these checks follow the path from design to code to observed behavior. Completion also requires recording which checks and integration actions were performed.
entries.editorial: We follow the capacity example from model to code and observed behavior. Completion also needs an account of performed checks and integration work.

entries.original: The typed model needs to be internally consistent. In the capacity example, the Calculation's Rule reference must resolve and bind every required parameter with a compatible type. Its record properties and Enum alternatives must resolve too. The separate reservation design would also need its authored Operation relationships.
entries.editorial: Internal consistency requires the Calculation’s Rule reference, every compatible parameter, record property and Enum variant to resolve. A separate reservation design would need its own authored Operation relationships too.

entries.original: These checks prevent an inconsistent declaration from being treated as a valid compilation input. They make particular omissions observable: the Rule may be present, but its required connection can still be missing. They establish internal consistency within the checked contracts; review must also ask whether those contracts cover the intended task.
entries.editorial: These checks expose particular omissions and inconsistent inputs. A Rule can exist while its required connection is missing. Internal consistency still leaves a review question: do the checked contracts cover the intended task?

entries.original: The target now implements a different decision. Exact target verification can compare it with the selected source and realization and reject the changed artifact as nonconforming.
entries.editorial: The edited target now implements a different decision. Exact verification can compare it against the selected source and realization and reject it as nonconforming.

entries.original: The same comparison addresses incomplete code. Replacing the decision body with an unconditional Accept, omitting the Reject branch or removing the bound Rule call changes the expected implementation. Adding persistence changes it too. The observer also compares the files in the selected target with the recorded artifact inventory, exposing missing files as well as unexpected ones.
entries.editorial: An unconditional Accept, omitted Reject branch, missing Rule call or added persistence changes the expected output. The observer also compares the selected target’s files with its recorded inventory, revealing missing and unexpected files.

entries.original: That inventory is for the selected generated target. It establishes which artifacts belong to that selection; it does not establish that every required part of the wider application has been implemented.
entries.editorial: That inventory belongs to the selected generated target. Wider application completeness needs an account of the other required work.

entries.original: Rust type checking alone would accept many such edits. The artifact check concerns fidelity to the selected design. Behavioral evaluation addresses another question: what does a particular implementation actually do under the chosen conditions?
entries.editorial: Rust types could permit many of those edits. Artifact comparison examines fidelity to the selected design. Behavioral evaluation examines execution under chosen conditions. Both are useful, for different questions.

entries.original: Exact output comparison can reveal drift; it does not independently prove that the compiler's translation rules are correct. Independent behavioral comparisons and formal checks can supply further evidence within their own stated scope.
entries.editorial: Exact output comparison identifies drift. Translation-rule correctness still needs independent behavioral or formal evidence within its stated scope.

entries.original: Exact verification concerns the selected artifact. A refactoring can preserve behavior while changing its representation, so accepting a different implementation form requires an explicit selection and applicable evidence. Fidelity to a selected output and suitability of the architecture for future changes remain separate review questions.
entries.editorial: A refactoring can preserve behavior while changing representation. Selecting a different form needs explicit selection and applicable evidence. Fidelity to the selected output and architectural suitability for future change stay separate review questions.

entries.original: The architectural contract defines the obligations. Checks exercise those obligations and report the affected subject, disagreement and evidence. Detection supports correction; it does not itself establish that correction has happened.
entries.editorial: The architectural contract gives checks their obligations. They report a subject, disagreement and evidence. Detection gives us something to correct, without establishing that the correction has occurred.

entries.original: The Rule becomes an executable comparison. The Calculation calls that Rule and selects its declared result. For request R-104 , 4 requested units compared with 5 available units must produce Accept. The equality and over-capacity cases exercise the other outcome.
entries.editorial: R-104 compares 4 requested units with 5 available and must return Accept through the bound Rule. Equality and over-capacity cases exercise Reject. The Calculation selects the result of the actual comparison.

entries.original: The equality case distinguishes the intended strict comparison from a more permissive one: both would accept 4/5, but they disagree at 5/5. Acceptance follows the bound Rule; the caller does not supply an arbitrary Boolean to stand in for the Rule.
entries.editorial: The equality case exposes a meaningful difference. Strict and permissive comparisons both accept 4/5, while disagreeing at 5/5. The bound Rule supplies acceptance; a caller-supplied Boolean cannot substitute for it.

entries.original: The existence of a check does not establish that an agent ran it. If the task requires observing the 4/5, 5/5 and 6/5 cases, the completion record needs results for the relevant implementation version. A check left unperformed remains an open obligation. If a caller update is also required, conformance of the decision artifact alone cannot establish that update.
entries.editorial: These results establish the observed behavior for selected targets, input quantities and toolchain conditions. Other callers, concurrency, integrations and environments need their own evidence.

entries.original: The original decision now gives us a reference for two different kinds of change: revising what acceptance means and adding behavior after acceptance.
entries.editorial: The decision now gives us a reference for two changes: revising acceptance’s meaning and adding behavior after acceptance. We should establish which change the request asks for.

entries.original: The definition must first change its acceptance boundary. The corresponding Rule expression and its expected boundary cases then need revision. Compilation translates the selected successor model into code, and new evidence concerns that successor. Earlier results remain evidence about their original inputs.
entries.editorial: Allowing equality changes the definition’s boundary, then the Rule and expected boundary cases. Compilation translates the selected successor. New evidence concerns that successor, while earlier results retain their original inputs and scope.

entries.original: A different request—“reserve capacity when the decision succeeds”—has wider consequences. It introduces state-changing behavior, ownership, concurrency and failure questions. Those responsibilities need their own declarations and applicable architecture constraints. They cannot be inferred from the existing Accept result.
entries.editorial: “Reserve capacity when the decision succeeds” adds state change, ownership, concurrency and failure questions. Those responsibilities need declarations and architecture constraints. Accept alone specifies none of that behavior.

entries.original: The convenient patch might decrement capacity inside the existing decision function. That would give a previously read-only responsibility a state-changing meaning and make every caller part of the reservation behavior. The model makes this change visible: writes, effects and failure behavior would now differ. Design review can require an explicit reservation responsibility before construction, with the relevant state owner and consistency rules.
entries.editorial: Decrementing capacity inside the classifier would change its read-only responsibility and affect every caller. Writes, effects and failure behavior would now differ. Review can require a separate reservation responsibility, with explicit state ownership and consistency, before construction.

entries.original: The distinction matters under concurrency. Two requests can each ask for 4 units while using snapshots that show 5 available. Each satisfies the original comparison, but reserving both would require 8 units. The reservation design needs to specify how the capacity check and state change remain consistent when requests overlap.
entries.editorial: Two requests might each ask for 4 while their snapshots show 5 available. Both satisfy the comparison, but reserving both requires 8. The reservation design needs a consistent check and state change when requests overlap.

entries.original: This is how a model guides evolution. It exposes which meaning changed, which responsibility was added, which declared dependencies follow and which evidence needs refreshing.
entries.editorial: The model helps us locate the evolution: the changed meaning, added responsibility, declared dependencies and evidence needing refresh. Those are the subjects of the next review.

entries.original: For an agent continuing the work, the change should begin with that explicit difference. Changing the Rust comparison and a test expectation together would still disagree with the original selected model. Changing the model without reviewing the business requirement would move the mistake into the source of construction. The review therefore concerns both the intended meaning and its implementation.
entries.editorial: A continuing agent should start with that difference. Changing a Rust comparison and its test still disagrees with the original model. Changing the model without examining the business requirement puts the mistake into the source. We need to review meaning and implementation together.

entries.original: Declared relationships help locate affected concepts. Consumers outside the graph still need to be identified and reviewed; a dependency absent from the model cannot contribute to that impact analysis.
entries.editorial: Declared relationships help find affected concepts. Consumers outside the graph still need identification and review. Missing dependencies contribute nothing to the model’s impact analysis.

entries.original: Retries are another everyday example. Stripe's API v1 binds an executed request's saved response to an idempotency key and compares parameters when that key is reused. A retry has an explicit identity and contract; sending the same payload again is not by itself the whole definition of repeating the same business operation. Stripe's idempotency documentation
entries.editorial: Retries supply another example. Stripe API v1 binds an executed request’s saved response to an idempotency key and checks parameters on reuse. Request identity and contract matter. Repeating a payload alone leaves the meaning of a repeated business operation unspecified.

entries.original: The design questions include which request identity is preserved, how long it is recognized, what happens after partial failure and which effects may be repeated. These details affect the meaning of the operation across its lifecycle, even when its function name stays the same.
entries.editorial: The design needs to establish request identity, recognition period, partial-failure behavior and repeatable effects. Those requirements shape the Operation across its lifecycle even when its function name is unchanged.

entries.original: Extensions to roles, relationships or implementation forms need to declare their scope and effects. Where an extension claims to preserve existing meaning, that claim needs examination under explicit conditions. Formal methods can establish selected preservation properties when their statements and assumptions are precise.
entries.editorial: Role, relationship and realization extensions need declared scope and effects. A claimed preservation of meaning needs examination under explicit conditions. Precise formal statements and assumptions can establish selected preservation properties.

entries.original: The previous sections show how the capacity decision is modeled, constructed and checked. Now consider how an agent continues that work when some of it is missing, and how later requests can affect the design.
entries.editorial: We have followed the capacity decision through modeling, construction and checks. Now consider an incomplete result and a later request changing the design. Both need to be recoverable by the next agent.

entries.original: Suppose an agent implements within_capacity and reports that capacity acceptance is finished. The helper contains the correct comparison, but the task also requires a Calculation that uses it and returns both decisions. The helper alone leaves a required connection and behavior unfinished.
entries.editorial: Suppose the agent implements within_capacity and reports completion. The comparison is correct, yet the required Calculation using it and returning both decisions is missing. The helper leaves connected behavior unfinished.

entries.original: Craft gives the work several places where that omission can be examined. The following is a walkthrough of the example, not a report of a newly executed run.
entries.editorial: The following walkthrough shows where Craft could expose that omission. It is an explanation of the example, rather than a newly executed run.

entries.original: The agent can trace the omission against the selected Calculation contract. Does the model contain the conditional decision and both outcomes? If a required typed dependency is absent, validation identifies a model problem. If the model is complete but the expected Calculation or a branch is missing from the selected generated target, artifact verification identifies an implementation disagreement.
entries.editorial: Start with the selected contract. Does the model declare the conditional decision and both outcomes? Missing typed dependencies are model problems. If the model is complete but the generated Calculation or a branch is missing, target verification exposes an implementation disagreement.

entries.original: The partial helper cannot become the completion criterion simply because it is the code the agent produced. The selected design supplies the expected output and file inventory. An API caller update, if included in the task, adds a separate obligation that must be recorded and designed where applicable. Compiling the decision does not perform that integration work.
entries.editorial: The helper alone does not become the criterion for completion. The selected design supplies required output and inventory. An API caller update included in the task is another obligation to record and design. Compiling the decision leaves that integration work to be performed.

entries.original: Behavioral evaluation has a separate purpose. The 4/5 case exercises acceptance, 5/5 checks the equality boundary, and 6/5 exercises rejection above capacity. A successful acceptance case alone gives no execution evidence for the other two. Their expected results remain visible even if an agent forgets to evaluate them.
entries.editorial: Evaluation also needs the other outcomes. 4/5 exercises Accept, 5/5 the equality boundary and 6/5 rejection above capacity. One successful acceptance case leaves the other cases unexamined, with their expected results still available to the next session.

entries.original: Imagine the decision artifact has been checked, but the equality case has not been evaluated and the API caller has not been updated. The next session needs those gaps alongside the work already performed. A useful project record would distinguish:
entries.editorial: Suppose the artifact was checked while the equality case and caller update are unfinished. The next session needs both the completed work and those gaps. Its project record should distinguish the following facts.

entries.original: These are the contents of an explanatory handoff, not a new Craft schema. They show why completion needs an account of obligations and evidence. The existence of conforming decision code cannot stand in for a caller update or an evaluation that has not happened.
entries.editorial: This handoff explains obligations and evidence, without introducing a new Craft schema. Conforming decision code leaves unperformed caller changes and evaluations to their own completion records.

entries.original: Once the decision's responsibilities are explicit, consider a sequence of requests to extend the service. Each request adds something the earlier design must now accommodate. The following is a design sketch of possible evolution; reservation and retry behavior are additional responsibilities beyond the compiled decision shown earlier.
entries.editorial: Now extend the service through several requests. Each introduces something the previous design must accommodate. This is a possible evolution sketch: reservation and retries add responsibilities beyond the compiled classifier.

entries.original: Each patch could satisfy a narrow example. Together, they make changes increasingly expensive: the next agent must find every copied rule, infer which flags matter and determine where an effect has already happened. Changing the acceptance boundary now requires coordinating several implementations instead of revising one declared responsibility. New fixes can then add another branch or copy, continuing the cycle.
entries.editorial: Individual patches could pass narrow examples while making the next change harder. The next agent would need to find copied rules, infer flags and establish which effects occurred. Changing acceptance could require coordinating several implementations. More exceptions can then deepen the same problem.

entries.original: With Craft, the design change should declare the new responsibility before choosing its implementation form:
entries.editorial: For Craft, begin by declaring the added responsibility before choosing its implementation form. That makes the proposed change available for review.

entries.original: The resulting questions are concrete. Can the API and worker reach the same declared decision? Who owns the capacity mutation? What happens when two requests observe the same available capacity? What evidence establishes that a retry cannot reserve twice? The original read-only decision cannot answer the last two questions; the reservation design must address them.
entries.editorial: The review questions become concrete. Do the API and worker use the same decision? Who owns mutation? How do overlapping requests stay consistent, and what prevents a retry from reserving twice? The reservation design must answer the state and retry questions beyond the original classifier’s scope.

entries.original: Craft contributes explicit responsibility roles, typed relationships and selected architecture constraints against which the proposed composition can be checked. Compilation constructs supported declarations through the selected implementation forms. Target verification can expose a direct patch to the original decision that adds a database decrement, because that patch differs from its selected output.
entries.editorial: Craft supplies responsibility roles, typed relationships and architecture constraints for checking the composition. Compilation constructs supported declarations in selected forms. Target verification can expose a database decrement patched into the original decision because it differs from the selected output.

entries.original: The wider design still needs review. A copied comparison in a handwritten worker outside the model is outside that artifact comparison, and a poorly chosen model or realization can encode an unsuitable architecture consistently. Keeping the graph, profiles and relevant consumer evidence current is part of maintaining the design. Deterministic construction does not establish that a design will remain easy to extend.
entries.editorial: The wider design still needs review. A handwritten worker’s copied comparison falls outside that target comparison. A poor model or realization can consistently encode a poor architecture. Maintaining the graph, profiles and consumer evidence matters alongside deterministic construction.

entries.original: A useful review therefore follows the sequence of changes. After each addition, examine whether ownership remains clear, rules have been duplicated, dependencies have crossed declared boundaries and failure behavior is still explicit. Evaluate the new behavior and the obligations inherited from earlier versions. Concentrated complexity, duplication and growing change effort can help identify areas needing redesign; they are signals to investigate rather than a complete measure of maintainability.
entries.editorial: Follow the sequence of changes. After each addition, examine ownership, duplicated rules, crossed boundaries and failure behavior. Evaluate new behavior and inherited obligations. Growing complexity, duplication or change effort are reasons to investigate redesign, with no single complete maintainability measure implied.

entries.original: The practical shift is that the agent works against a design that persists beyond the session. It can propose changes, investigate disagreements and identify missing work using the selected contracts and recorded observations. Earlier shortcuts and unresolved design questions should also remain visible, so the next session can address them rather than unknowingly building another workaround on top.
entries.editorial: The agent works from a design that persists beyond its session. Selected contracts and observations let it propose changes, investigate disagreements and identify missing work. Earlier shortcuts and unresolved questions should remain visible for the next session too.

entries.original: Its model still needs review: compilation can faithfully implement an incomplete, incorrect or difficult-to-maintain design. The aim is to make design choices and their consequences explicit enough to examine before they become the foundation for further work.
entries.editorial: Compilation can faithfully construct an incomplete, incorrect or difficult design. Review still needs to examine the choices and consequences before later work depends on them.

entries.original: Within the Lab, the machine agent is ephemeral. Its session can have short-term memory. Durable design knowledge belongs to Project State, retained through explicit governed writes. Context Views select information relevant to the task; Ontology Views select relevant concepts and relationships with exact source versions and use conditions. They are derived selections, not a second canonical store. A later session obtains new checked views and current permission rather than extending an expired view or delegation. The selected compiler inputs, completed work, observed results and remaining obligations can then inform its next assignment.
entries.editorial: In the Lab, a machine agent is ephemeral and working memory belongs to its session. Durable design knowledge enters Project State through governed writes. Context and Ontology Views select relevant information and connections with exact sources and use conditions. They supply derived selections. A later session needs fresh checked views and current permission, using compiler inputs, results and open obligations for its new assignment.

entries.original: CyberAlchemy Lab organizes knowledge and work. Craft contributes a specialized model for software design, architectural composition, code compilation and implementation conformance—the comparison of an observed implementation with its selected design.
entries.editorial: The Lab organizes knowledge and work. Craft specializes software design, composition, compilation and implementation conformance: comparing an observed implementation with its selected design.

entries.original: Craft is a Product with its own software-design promise. A project using Craft can be working on another Product. In the Lab guide's Northstar incident , that other Product is the customer-data platform, and the Project coordinates its export repair. Craft could supply software-modeling and construction tools for a later repair Work item. It would not become the customer platform or the repair Project.
entries.editorial: Craft has its own Product promise. A project using it might work on another Product, such as Northstar’s customer-data platform. The Project coordinates export repair. Craft could supply tools for later repair Work while retaining its own identity.

entries.original: The incident's current task is investigation: compare the saved export with the required identifiers under the accepted account, filters and snapshot. A later authorized implementation task could express that criterion in a Craft Rule and model the retrieval responsibilities and their permitted connections. Its architecture selections and supported contracts would govern construction. Generated code and check results would return to the repair work as identifiable outputs with a source trail. Evidence of repair, adoption, activation and incident closure would still need their own records and decisions. This is a possible use of Craft, not a report that it compiled or repaired the Northstar example.
entries.editorial: Northstar’s current task is investigation under the accepted account, filters and snapshot. Later authorized implementation could express the criterion as a Craft Rule and model retrieval responsibilities and permitted connections. Profiles and supported contracts would govern construction. Code and checks would return as traceable outputs. Repair evidence, adoption, activation and closure would follow their own routes. This describes possible use, without claiming an executed Northstar compilation or repair.

entries.original: The capacity example connects several different subjects: a definition, a software model, source-code artifacts and records of work and observations. The Lab connects those subjects so that the next person or agent can understand their meaning, origin and current state.
entries.editorial: The capacity example involves a definition, software model, code artifacts and records of work and observations. The Lab connects them so the next participant can recover their meaning, origin and current state.

entries.original: The Lab and Craft retain distinct contracts. A business definition and the Rule implementing its predicate need an explicit, versioned correspondence under the applicable contract. Equal labels alone do not establish that correspondence. The Calculation's Rule reference belongs to Craft's software contract. A future Rule-to-reservation enforces edge would belong to Craft's relationship model. Connections among Lab definition, Work and evidence records belong to the Lab artifact model.
entries.editorial: A business definition and its implementing Rule need explicit versioned correspondence under the applicable contract. Equal labels leave that correspondence to be established. The Calculation’s Rule reference and a future enforces link belong to Craft’s contracts. Connections among Lab definitions, Work and evidence belong to the Lab model.

entries.original: The Lab's admitted Workflow definition uses the same software meaning: ordered orchestration of Operations within or across Product Feature boundaries. A Work item may ask an agent to design, construct or evaluate that Workflow. Evaluation can produce a recovery intent and plan; invoking exact Operation bindings belongs to a separate executor. Retaining a workflow declaration as a governed record does not turn it into a general project plan.
entries.editorial: The admitted Lab Workflow meaning is software orchestration of Operations within or across Product Feature boundaries. Work can ask an agent to design, build or evaluate it. Evaluation can produce recovery intent and plan; a separate executor invokes Operation bindings. Recording the declaration does not make it a general project plan.

entries.original: An ontology can represent the software model and its connections with explicit source bindings and a declared local contract. A Lab Ontology View selects such records for a purpose; it does not replace their authority or turn local connections into global ones. The Lab guide's connection rules explain why a new global connection needs its own admitted contract. A Craft feature is an organization unit; it does not by itself establish a Lab Bounded Context.
entries.editorial: An ontology can represent software concepts and connections under a declared local contract with source bindings. A Lab Ontology View selects them for a purpose while preserving authority and the distinction between local and global connections. A global extension needs an admitted contract. A Craft feature alone establishes no Lab Bounded Context.

entries.original: The three axes also make an agent's handoff interpretable. Authority identifies its governing definitions, contracts and permission to act. Provenance connects the code and evaluation results to their exact inputs and responsible actions. Lifecycle records whether a proposal, artifact or Work item has reached the applicable state through its required transitions.
entries.editorial: The three governance questions also help us read a handoff. Authority supplies governing meanings, contracts and permission. Provenance connects code and results to exact inputs and responsible actions. Lifecycle records each subject’s state through required transitions.

entries.original: Each state belongs to a particular subject. The model's acceptance, an evaluation's progress and a compute job's execution are different lifecycle questions. Keeping the subject visible prevents one status from being used to describe all three.
entries.editorial: Model acceptance, evaluation progress and compute-job execution are different subjects. Keeping the subject visible lets a reader understand which state a status describes.

entries.original: A successful check supports a scoped claim. Approving a design change or permitting deployment remains a separate authorized decision. An agent's statement that the work is complete must be assessed against the applicable obligations and evidence.
entries.editorial: A successful check supplies a scoped claim. Design approval or deployment permission requires a separate authorized decision. An agent’s completion report is assessed against the applicable obligations and evidence.

entries.original: Deployment can introduce another disagreement between intended and observed state. In the 2012 Knight Capital incident, a deployment missed one of eight servers. A repurposed flag activated obsolete behavior on that server. The SEC's account illustrates why artifact identity, version compatibility and actual deployment state matter alongside the design and code. SEC findings, 2013
entries.editorial: Deployment can disagree with intended state too. In Knight Capital’s 2012 incident, one of eight servers missed a deployment and a repurposed flag activated obsolete behavior there. The SEC’s account gives a concrete reason to examine artifact identity, compatibility and actual deployment alongside design and code.

entries.original: A claim that code follows a model therefore needs a named target and version. Whether every running target has that code, and whether its surrounding operational contracts hold, requires further observation.
entries.editorial: A conformance claim needs a named target and version. Whether every running target has those bytes and meets its operational contracts needs further observation.

entries.original: We are building Craft so that design has a traceable consequence in software: domain meaning informs the model; architectural selections constrain its composition; the compiler translates the supported design into code; checks reveal whether the observed target respects that selection.
entries.editorial: We’re building Craft to give design a traceable consequence in software. Domain meaning informs the model, architecture constrains composition, and supported translations produce code. Checks then examine whether an observed target follows that selection.

entries.original: The shared documentation site makes those explanations navigable together. It does not establish that the Lab runtime already executes Craft tools, records every compiler output or continuously refreshes an ontology of every project object. Those integrations require explicit tool and implementation selections, recording contracts, authorized actions and evidence. The Lab's operational-scope section describes its inspected runtime snapshot separately from this Craft development article.
entries.editorial: The shared site lets readers follow those explanations together. It establishes no automatic Lab execution of Craft tools, recording of every output or continuous ontology refresh. Those integrations need selections, recording contracts, authorization and evidence. The Lab’s operational-scope page keeps its inspected runtime snapshot separate from this development article.

entries.original: For agentic engineering, this reduces the work that depends on repeatedly reconstructing design intent and manually assembling declared behavior. It also provides a reference for investigating omissions and drift. Requirements must still be modeled, checks must still be performed, and wider integration needs its own evidence. The closed-beta work is focused on developing and examining this supported scope.
entries.editorial: For agent work, the supported scope reduces repeated reconstruction and manual assembly of declared behavior. It also supplies a reference for omissions and drift. Requirements still need modeling, checks need execution and integrations need their own evidence. The closed beta focuses on developing and examining that scope.

entries.original: Organize your company’s knowledge and work, so people and AI agents share the context behind each decision.
entries.editorial: Organize your company’s knowledge and work, so people and AI agents share the context behind each decision.

entries.original: For software work, Craft makes concepts, rules and behavior explicit, giving implementation a model to work from.
entries.editorial: For software work, Craft makes concepts, rules and behavior explicit, giving implementation a model to work from.

entries.original: Select a part to explore its role. Select it again to return to the whole.
entries.editorial: Choose a part to explore its responsibility. Select it again when you want the full picture.

entries.original: People express intentions and review results. Agents act within their permissions. The project keeps the meanings, evidence and decisions that let the work continue.
entries.editorial: People express intentions and review results. Agents work within permission. The project retains the meanings, evidence and decisions needed to continue.

entries.original: A project carries more than tasks. It carries the meaning of its goals, the reasoning behind its decisions and the evidence of what happened.
entries.editorial: A task list leaves some important questions open. What do the goals mean? Why was a decision taken, and what evidence supports the account of what happened? The project needs those answers too.

entries.original: The Lab gives that knowledge a continuing structure. Definitions state what important terms mean. Connected records show what was attempted, which evidence supports a claim and which decisions govern a change.
entries.editorial: The Lab gives that knowledge a continuing structure. Definitions state the important meanings. Connected records let the next reader inspect attempts, claim support and decisions governing change.

entries.original: When work changes hands, the next person or agent has a place to recover those connections.
entries.editorial: When the work changes hands, those connections give the next participant a place to begin.

entries.original: Express the intention and define the terms that determine success. “Complete” needs a criterion that everyone can examine.
entries.editorial: Start with the intention and the meaning of success. If the task says “complete,” give people a criterion they can examine.

entries.original: Identify the sources, methods and observations behind an assessment. Keep a finding connected to what supports it.
entries.editorial: Follow an assessment back to its sources, methods and observations. The finding should stay connected to its actual support.

entries.original: A proposal, an accepted change and a deployment have different effects. Each follows its declared rules and authority.
entries.editorial: Proposing a change, accepting it and deploying it have different consequences. Each needs its declared rules and authority.

entries.original: Give the next session the relevant project knowledge. Check that its context and permissions still apply before continuing.
entries.editorial: The next session needs relevant project knowledge, usable context and current permission. Check those before continuing.

entries.original: An agent session is temporary. The knowledge needed to continue the work belongs to the project.
entries.editorial: An agent session ends. The knowledge needed to continue belongs in the project.

entries.original: The Lab organizes that durable knowledge as project state. Context views select the information needed for a task; ontology views show relevant concepts and their declared connections. A new session recovers its context from those views.
entries.editorial: Project State keeps that knowledge. Context Views select information for a task, and Ontology Views show relevant concepts and declared connections. A fresh session recovers context through those views.

entries.original: Short-term memory belongs to the session. If a view expires or permission no longer applies, the agent refreshes its context or pauses. Persisting a lesson also creates something to examine: later work needs evidence of its use and benefit.
entries.editorial: Working memory belongs to the session. Expired views or changed permissions require refresh or a pause. A saved lesson also needs examination: later work should record its use and assess its benefit.

entries.original: Built by CyberAlchemy, a research lab investigating intelligence and how people and machines work together. Our research, culture and ambition →
entries.editorial: CyberAlchemy is a research lab studying intelligence and how people and machines work together. Our research, culture and ambition →

entries.original: Keep the meaning, evidence and decisions behind work available to the next person—and the next agent.
entries.editorial: Keep the meanings, evidence and decisions behind work available to whoever continues it, including the next agent.

entries.original: A customer reports a problem. Someone investigates it, reads the logs, forms a hypothesis and proposes a change. A colleague returns the next morning. Before doing useful work, they need to recover what happened: which data was examined, what “fixed” would mean, why a change was proposed and who can approve it.
entries.editorial: A customer reports a problem. Someone reads logs, forms a hypothesis and proposes a change. A colleague returns the following morning and needs to recover the basis: the data examined, what “fixed” means, why the proposal exists and who can approve it. That recovery is work in its own right.

entries.original: Add AI agents to that process and the question becomes more pressing. A session can produce code, an assessment or a plan. The next session still needs a reliable account of what that work means. A convincing explanation gives a reviewer something to read; a connected record gives them something to examine.
entries.editorial: An agent session can leave code, an assessment or a plan. The next session needs an account of its meaning and status. A connected record lets a reviewer examine the basis of the explanation, rather than depend on how convincing it sounds.

entries.original: CyberAlchemy Lab is being built for teams whose work depends on that continuity: software teams, research groups and operations teams coordinating people and agents across projects.
entries.editorial: We’re building the Lab for software, research and operations teams coordinating people and agents across projects. Continuity is part of their work.

entries.original: We call CyberAlchemy Lab an open-source company brain system . The name describes a practical ambition: keep knowledge connected to the work it informs, with enough structure for people and machines to inspect it.
entries.editorial: We call the Lab an open-source company brain system. The ambition is practical: connect knowledge to the work it informs with enough structure for people and machines to inspect it.

entries.original: That knowledge includes the meaning of important terms, the intentions behind a project, the evidence collected during work and the decisions that change what is accepted. The system organizes these as explicit records and declared connections.
entries.editorial: That knowledge includes important meanings, project intentions, evidence gathered and decisions changing what is accepted. Records and declared connections give those facts identifiable places.

entries.original: A document store can preserve an explanation. The Lab model asks further questions about its role: does it define a meaning, record an observation, propose a change or authorize an effect? Each has different requirements. Making those roles explicit helps the next reader know how the information may be used.
entries.editorial: When reading a saved explanation, we still need to understand its role. Is it defining a meaning, recording an observation, proposing a change or authorizing an effect? Those roles have different requirements and limits on use.

entries.original: The Lab begins with definitions. When a project depends on “complete,” “valid” or “recovered,” those words need boundaries. An accepted definition gives an exact meaning authority within a declared scope. The associated record format expresses how that meaning is represented.
entries.editorial: The Lab starts with definitions. “Complete,” “valid” and “recovered” need boundaries when work depends on them. An accountable owner accepts an exact meaning within scope; the associated record format governs its representation.

entries.original: Together, these questions let a team examine a claim and the proposed response. Evidence supports an assessment; an accountable decision determines the permitted change. A proposed fix remains a proposal until it follows its applicable review and authority route.
entries.editorial: Now a team has a basis for examining the claim and response. Evidence supports the assessment. An accountable decision authorizes a change. A proposed fix stays proposed until its applicable route is completed.

entries.original: The intent explains what the team wants to accomplish. A product describes the continuing purpose of a system. A project coordinates work toward a bounded change. Work records describe the attempts made along the way. These distinctions keep the purpose visible as individual tasks move forward.
entries.editorial: Intent gives the work a purpose. Product identifies a continuing offering, Project coordinates a bounded effort, and Work records its attempts. Individual tasks can then move ahead while their purpose remains recoverable.

entries.original: Consider the fictional Northstar incident in the guide. A customer says its data export is missing records. An agent receives a bounded investigation assignment: inspect the saved source snapshot, output and logs; compare identifiers; record candidate assessment material; and prepare a proposal.
entries.editorial: In the fictional Northstar case, a customer reports missing export records. The agent’s bounded investigation covers saved sources, output and logs, identifier comparison, candidate assessment material and a proposal.

entries.original: The definition of completeness fixes the account, filters and source snapshot. The comparison can therefore establish a specific omission. The cause, wider impact and recovery still need investigation.
entries.editorial: The completeness definition fixes account, filters and snapshot. That lets the comparison establish a scoped omission. Cause, wider impact and recovery still need investigation.

entries.original: The assignment also makes the agent’s boundary clear. Preparing a change proposal falls within the investigation. Changing source data, deploying a fix, accepting a definition or closing the incident requires the relevant separate authority.
entries.editorial: The assignment identifies investigation. Permission to change source data, deploy a fix, accept a definition or close the incident has to come from the relevant authority route.

entries.original: The result is an inspectable chain: an explicit criterion, identified inputs, a recorded comparison and a scoped proposal. The next reviewer can examine each part. Follow the full incident walkthrough .
entries.editorial: A reviewer can follow the criterion, inputs, comparison and proposal. Each part has a basis to examine. The full walkthrough follows that account.

entries.original: Machine agents are temporary. Their short-term memory belongs to the session. Continuing knowledge belongs to the project state: the durable records of meaning, work, evidence and decisions.
entries.editorial: A machine agent is temporary, with working memory belonging to its session. Project State retains the meanings, work, evidence and decisions another session needs.

entries.original: Each new session receives a context view suited to its task. An ontology view shows the relevant concepts and their declared connections. Both come from project state and have conditions for use. If a view expires, the agent must refresh it or pause. Continuing the work requires usable context and applicable permission.
entries.editorial: Each session gets a task-specific Context View and a relevant Ontology View. Both derive from Project State and declare use conditions. If a view expires, the agent refreshes or pauses. Continuing needs usable information and current permission.

entries.original: This is also where learning becomes a research question. A saved lesson can be examined and tried in later work. Claims of improvement need evidence of its actual use and an assessment of the observed benefit.
entries.editorial: Learning is another question to examine. A saved lesson can be tried in later work. To claim improvement, we need evidence of actual use and an assessment of the resulting benefit.

entries.original: AI alignment concerns whether machine behavior follows human intentions and values. These are difficult to express completely, and people can disagree about them. The research spans how systems are trained, how their behavior is evaluated and how they can be controlled. Ji et al., AI Alignment: A Comprehensive Survey .
entries.editorial: AI alignment examines whether behavior follows human intentions and values. Expressing those fully is difficult, and people disagree. Training, evaluation and control are parts of that research.
