entries.original: The Lab gives us a place to investigate part of that problem. Can clearer meanings reduce misunderstandings? Can scoped permissions and visible evidence help people detect a bad action sooner? Can project state preserve corrections across changing agents?
entries.editorial: The Lab gives us a setting for some of those questions. Do clearer meanings reduce misunderstandings? Would bounded permissions and visible evidence help expose a bad action sooner? Can Project State preserve corrections as agents change?

entries.original: Those are research questions we can formulate and test. Governance records make intentions and decisions inspectable. Establishing how an agent actually behaves calls for evaluation under changing conditions, adversarial exercises and continuing oversight. Anthropic’s alignment research describes those complementary lines of inquiry.
entries.editorial: We can formulate and test those questions. Governance records make intentions and decisions inspectable. Actual behavior needs evaluation under changing conditions, adversarial exercises and oversight. These are complementary lines of research.

entries.original: Our ambition toward more general intelligence belongs beside this work. As a machine’s capabilities expand, our ability to express direction, examine behavior and revise the course must develop with them.
entries.editorial: More general intelligence is part of the ambition. As capabilities grow, we need better ways to express direction, examine behavior and change course.

entries.original: Take a project where people routinely reconstruct context. Ask what its important words mean, which evidence supports its current claims and who may make the next change. Those questions offer a concrete starting point for understanding the Lab.
entries.editorial: Choose a project where people keep rebuilding context. Ask what its important words mean, what supports current claims and who is allowed to make the next change. That gives us a concrete place to begin.

entries.original: The documentation lets you examine the model through a guided incident, a visual system map and the complete reference library. If your question concerns software behavior, Craft shows how explicit models can express it within the wider Lab.
entries.editorial: The incident, system map and reference library provide routes into the model. For software behavior, the Craft article follows explicit design within the wider Lab.

entries.original: Through cybernetics, scientific inquiry and software, we work to turn intentions into understandable, governable systems—even when the AI within them is imperfect and probabilistic.
entries.editorial: We use cybernetics, scientific inquiry and software to work toward understandable, governable systems. Imperfect, probabilistic AI makes the questions harder, rather than removing the need to examine them.

entries.original: Alchemy gave us an image: transforming what we have into something we have yet to understand how to make.
entries.editorial: Alchemy gave us an image of transformation: starting with something available and working toward something we do not yet know how to make.

entries.original: Our starting material is an intention—something we want to understand, change or create. We work to turn it into knowledge, models and systems that others can examine and use.
entries.editorial: We start with an intention, something to understand, change or create. The work is to express it as knowledge, models and systems another participant can examine and use.

entries.original: Cybernetics gives us a way to study that transformation: observe what happens, compare it with what was intended, respond to the difference and revise our understanding.
entries.editorial: Cybernetics gives us a way to study that work. Observe the result, compare it with the intention, respond to the difference and reconsider the understanding behind it.

entries.original: The name brings that possibility and responsibility together. We want to transform things. We want to understand what we are transforming.
entries.editorial: The name holds an ambition and a responsibility together. We want to transform things, and we want to understand what we are changing.

entries.original: We are a band of deviants and renegades. Curiosity leads us into subjects we do not yet understand.
entries.editorial: We describe ourselves as a band of deviants and renegades. Curiosity takes us into subjects we still need to learn.

entries.original: We begin by learning. We make our assumptions visible and put our ideas against evidence and criticism. Finding ourselves wrong is part of the work. What matters is whether we notice, understand why and change our course.
entries.editorial: Learning comes first. We expose assumptions and let evidence and criticism challenge our ideas. Being wrong belongs in the work. We need to notice, understand the mistake and change course.

entries.original: We study reality with the intention of expressing parts of it in machines. That requires understanding our models, their limits and ourselves.
entries.editorial: We study reality with the intention of expressing parts of it in machines. Our models, their limits and our own judgments need examination too.

entries.original: A company accumulates knowledge through people, projects, decisions and mistakes. Keeping that knowledge useful is a continuing task.
entries.editorial: A company accumulates knowledge through projects, people, decisions and mistakes. Keeping it useful requires continuing work.

entries.original: CyberAlchemy Lab organizes knowledge and work around explicit definitions, traceable evidence and declared rules for change. People and agents can recover what a project means, what supports its current state and what they may do next.
entries.editorial: The Lab organizes that knowledge around definitions, evidence and declared change rules. People and agents can recover project meaning, claim support and permission for the next action.

entries.original: Our ambition reaches toward more general artificial intelligence. It begins with questions about human learning, intention, culture and judgment.
entries.editorial: Our ambition includes more general artificial intelligence. Questions about learning, intention, culture and judgment are a place to start.

entries.original: That ambition brings alignment into the same inquiry: how can AI behavior remain responsive to human intentions and values as systems become more capable? People disagree, situations change and a stated goal can leave important things unsaid. Read the alignment survey .
entries.editorial: Alignment belongs in that inquiry. How does increasingly capable AI stay responsive to human intentions and values when people disagree, circumstances change and a stated goal leaves things unsaid?

entries.original: We investigate how intentions can be expressed, behavior examined and mistakes corrected. The Lab gives these questions a practical setting: explicit meanings, bounded permissions, evidence and accountable changes.
entries.editorial: We study how to express intentions, examine behavior and correct mistakes. The Lab provides a practical setting with explicit meanings, bounded permissions, evidence and accountable changes.

entries.original: These structures help us formulate and examine alignment questions. Establishing that a machine behaves well requires evaluation, stress testing and oversight of its actual behavior. Explore research on evaluation and oversight .
entries.editorial: Those structures help us formulate the questions. Establishing good behavior still requires evaluation, stress testing and oversight of actual execution.

entries.original: A first reading of the ideas that organize knowledge and work in CyberAlchemy Lab.
entries.editorial: Begin with the ideas behind knowledge and work in the Lab, then follow the parts you need in more detail.

entries.original: CyberAlchemy is a system for organizing knowledge and work. It connects what things mean, why work matters, what was done and what can happen next. People and agents can recover those connections instead of reconstructing them from scattered conversations.
entries.editorial: CyberAlchemy organizes knowledge and work. It connects meaning, purpose, performed work and possible next changes. A returning person or agent has records to examine instead of reconstructing everything from conversations.

entries.original: Consider a customer reporting an incomplete data export. Investigating it requires a meaning for “complete,” access to the relevant data, a comparison that can be examined and a decision about the response. The Lab gives each of these a place in the same body of knowledge.
entries.editorial: Consider an incomplete export report. We need a meaning for “complete,” permission for relevant data, an inspectable comparison and a response decision. The Lab gives each responsibility a place in the same project knowledge.

entries.original: The guide follows this through the fictional Northstar incident . This introduction gives you the concepts needed to follow it.
entries.editorial: The guide follows the fictional Northstar incident. This page introduces the concepts used in that investigation.

entries.original: Definitions make the basic meanings and boundaries explicit. An accepted definition is a basic unit of authority over meaning: an accountable owner has accepted an exact version for a declared purpose and scope.
entries.editorial: A definition states meaning and boundaries. An accepted exact version is a basic unit of authority over meaning within an accountable owner’s declared purpose and scope.

entries.original: For the export investigation, “complete” means that every required row identifier from the declared account, filters and fixed source snapshot appears in the saved output. That criterion lets the agent assess identifier coverage. Accuracy of the values and permission to access the data have their own requirements.
entries.editorial: For this export, completeness requires every selected identifier from the declared account, filters and fixed snapshot in the saved output. That examines identifier coverage. Value accuracy and data-access permission need their own requirements.

entries.original: Connections between records also follow declared rules. An Ontology View represents selected subjects and connections as a graph, preserving their identities and the source on which the view depends.
entries.editorial: Connections also have rules. An Ontology View displays selected subjects and relationships while retaining identities and the sources it depends on.

entries.original: These questions stay connected throughout the work. Evidence supports a conclusion within its scope; permission governs the requested action; a recorded transition preserves the resulting state.
entries.editorial: The three questions stay with the work. Evidence supports a scoped conclusion, permission governs an action, and a transition records a resulting state.

entries.original: The Lab keeps the purpose, promised outcome and particular effort identifiable. Read these roles through the same incident:
entries.editorial: Purpose, promised outcome and particular effort need separate identities. Follow those responsibilities through the incident.

entries.original: Customers need their complete eligible data. An Intent Resolution selects a response and how to assess satisfaction.
entries.editorial: Customers need their complete eligible data. Intent Resolution selects a response and a way to assess whether it satisfies that need.

entries.original: The customer-data platform enables exports through a Product Capability. Specific implementations realize that outcome.
entries.editorial: The platform promises eligible export through a Product Capability. Particular implementations realize the outcome.

entries.original: The export-repair Project organizes the effort. Its Goal states the desired outcome and the evidence needed to establish success.
entries.editorial: The repair Project coordinates the effort. Its Goal states the outcome and evidence needed for achievement.

entries.original: Bind an agent to that investigation. Establish its permission separately through the applicable authority or delegation.
entries.editorial: Assignment binds the agent to investigation. Permission comes separately from the applicable authority or delegation.

entries.original: A machine agent works in a temporary Agent Session . A Context View prepares selected task information; an Ontology View provides a purpose-specific view of the connected model. Their source versions, limits and refresh conditions remain explicit.
entries.editorial: An Agent Session is temporary. Context View supplies task information, while Ontology View selects relevant concepts and connections. Both identify source versions, limits and refresh conditions.

entries.original: Long-term continuity comes from Project State : saved records, definitions, decisions, evidence, relationships and histories. Short-term working memory belongs to the session. When a machine agent session ends, its instance ends too; a later session recovers durable knowledge through newly checked views.
entries.editorial: Project State supplies continuity through saved meanings, records, decisions, evidence, connections and histories. Working memory belongs to one session. When that machine session ends, its instance ends too. A later agent recovers durable knowledge through fresh checked views.

entries.original: In the incident, the identifier comparison can survive the session. A later agent can inspect its basis and continue investigating the cause. A proposed lesson can also be retained, then examined through evidence of later use and benefit.
entries.editorial: The identifier comparison can survive the session, so another agent can inspect its basis and continue investigating cause. A saved lesson can also be examined through later use and benefit evidence.

entries.original: Craft is the software-design Product within the broader Lab model. A project can use its tools to express software responsibilities, architectural constraints and supported model-to-code construction.
entries.editorial: Craft is the software-design Product within the Lab. Its tools express responsibilities, architecture constraints and supported construction from model to code.

entries.original: Its model distinguishes a Rule that evaluates a condition, a Calculation that derives a value, a Query that retrieves information and an Operation that owns a business state change. In Craft’s capacity example, a Calculation returns Accept when the request is strictly below the supplied available capacity. Reserving that capacity belongs to a separate Operation.
entries.editorial: Craft separates a Rule’s condition, a Calculation’s derived value, a Query’s retrieval and an Operation’s state change. In its capacity example, the classifier accepts only a request strictly below supplied capacity. Reserving capacity is a separate Operation.

entries.original: The Craft software model describes the design and its implementation. The Lab connects that work with its purpose, ownership, evidence and decisions. Generated code and checks can become outputs of the work; accepting records and authorizing deployment follow their own authority routes.
entries.editorial: The Craft model describes design and implementation. Lab records connect that work to purpose, ownership, evidence and decisions. Generated code and checks can be Work outputs, with acceptance and deployment governed through their own authority routes.

entries.original: A customer reports missing records. Follow what an agent needs, what it can establish and how the next decision becomes reviewable.
entries.editorial: A customer reports missing export records. Follow the information and permission an agent needs, the claim it can establish and the owner’s next review.

entries.original: The report starts a response. It does not yet establish what went wrong. The service owner needs an investigation that can distinguish missing identifiers from an incorrect filter, a changed source or a mistaken expectation.
entries.editorial: The report starts a response. The investigation still has to distinguish missing identifiers from an incorrect filter, source change or mistaken expectation. The service owner needs evidence for that distinction.

entries.original: Read left to right, or top to bottom on a narrow screen. Numbers show the order of this explanation. They do not declare connections between Lab records.
entries.editorial: Read left to right, or top to bottom on a phone. The numbers order this explanation. Actual Lab connections use their declared contracts.

entries.original: The customer-data platform is the Product . Exporting eligible customer data is one of its capabilities. The repair Project coordinates the response; the investigation is a bounded Work item. An Agent Assignment identifies the agent’s job.
entries.editorial: The platform is the Product and eligible export is a capability. The repair Project coordinates the effort. Investigation is bounded Work, with an Agent Assignment recording its job.

entries.original: This is the case’s definition illustration. The Definition contract additionally requires its exact identity, owner, voices, boundaries and other governed fields; this annotated excerpt helps read those responsibilities.
entries.editorial: This excerpt illustrates the case’s definition. The complete contract also requires identity, owner, voices, boundaries and governed fields. Use the annotations to understand those responsibilities.

entries.original: Changing source data, deploying code, admitting a definition and closing the incident each require their applicable authority. An assignment alone supplies none of those permissions.
entries.editorial: Source changes, deployment, definition admission and incident closure require the authority applicable to each effect. Assignment records the job and supplies no such permissions.

entries.original: Use the values in fixed snapshot S1 to select Northstar’s active records. Then compare their stable identifiers with E12. Comparing row counts alone would miss duplicates or a different set of identifiers.
entries.editorial: Use S1’s values to select Northstar’s active records, then compare stable identifiers with E12. Counts alone could hide duplicates or a different identifier set.

entries.original: The observation records what happened. The method, selected data and result make it examinable. A new snapshot or changed filter would need its own comparison.
entries.editorial: The observation records what happened. Method, selected data and result give another reader a basis to examine it. New snapshots or filters need separate comparisons.

entries.original: The agent assembles an Evidence Set for the omission claim. A Failure Assessment evaluates the occurrence, mode, cause, impact, containment, recovery and uncertainty independently.
entries.editorial: An Evidence Set supports the scoped omission claim. Failure Assessment separately examines occurrence, mode, cause, impact, containment, recovery and uncertainty.

entries.original: Arrows name actual permitted ordered kind pairs. A saved connection must also satisfy its full contract, including exact endpoint references. These signatures are not complete validated instances.
entries.editorial: The arrows name permitted ordered kind pairs. An actual connection still needs the full contract, including exact endpoints. The signatures here are examples rather than validated instances.

entries.original: The case includes proposed software revision 8. Its repair effect has not been established. A useful proposal identifies what would change, the suspected mechanism, how to assess it, the affected scope and unresolved questions.
entries.editorial: Revision 8 is proposed, with repair efficacy still unestablished. A useful proposal names the change, suspected mechanism, assessment, scope and open questions.

entries.original: This is a conditional process illustration. The Northstar case stops before these results are established.
entries.editorial: These are conditional next steps. The fictional case has yet to establish their results.

entries.original: Craft can help express and construct the software change. Generated code and checks can become Work outputs. Their existence does not admit Lab records or authorize deployment.
entries.editorial: Craft could help express and construct a later software change. Its code and checks would be Work outputs. Record admission and deployment still need their own authority.

link_labels.Craft can help express and construct the: Craft could help express and construct a later software change.

entries.original: At 10:10, task view 3 has expired. The agent pauses because it cannot rely on that view for the next action. This does not mean its 30-minute delegation has necessarily expired; view usability and permission have separate conditions.
entries.editorial: At 10:10, view 3 expires and the agent pauses. That says something about information usability, without necessarily ending the 30-minute delegation. Continuing needs both checks.

entries.original: Read top to bottom: permitted writes preserve knowledge; newly checked views select it for later work. No session memory or authority is transferred by this diagram.
entries.editorial: Permitted writes save knowledge; newly checked views select it for later work. The diagram transfers neither session memory nor authority.

entries.original: The next agent can recover the 200-identifier omission and the candidate proposal. It still needs to investigate cause, establish wider impact and assess any recovery. Continuity preserves both knowledge and its limits.
entries.editorial: The next agent can recover the 200-identifier omission and proposal. Cause, wider impact and recovery still need examination. Continuity preserves those limits alongside the result.

entries.original: Use the same Northstar incident to see the distinct responsibility of each concept—and the conclusions it can support.
entries.editorial: Read the concepts through Northstar’s incident. Each has a responsibility and a boundary on what follows from its records.

entries.original: A definition, a type contract and a record answer successive questions. Keeping them identifiable lets meaning remain stable across many records and lets formats evolve through their own governed versions.
entries.editorial: Meaning, record format and a particular instance answer different questions. Keeping them identifiable lets formats evolve under their own version rules while preserving the governing meaning.

entries.original: Check the boundary: a schema-valid definition can still lack acceptance. An accepted type contract does not accept every instance that uses it. A new display or diagram does not change the underlying meaning.
entries.editorial: A valid structure can still await definition acceptance. An accepted type leaves each instance to its own standing. A new display leaves the underlying meaning unchanged.

entries.original: Check the boundary: finishing an investigation does not establish that a Product promise was fulfilled or a repair Goal achieved. Those conclusions need their own criteria, evidence and transitions.
entries.editorial: Finishing investigation supplies a Work result. Product delivery and repair-goal achievement need their own criteria, evidence and transitions.

entries.original: Check the boundary: an observation is not automatically sufficient evidence for every claim. An omission assessment does not establish a pagination defect or successful repair. A Decision chooses a response through its applicable authority.
entries.editorial: An observation supports particular claims under conditions. The omission leaves pagination cause and repair to be established. A Decision chooses a response under the applicable authority.

entries.original: Check the boundary: the agent needs both an assignment and applicable permission. Knowing what “complete” means does not grant data access, deployment or incident closure authority.
entries.editorial: The agent needs assignment and current permission. Knowing completeness’s meaning supplies no automatic data access, deployment or closure authority.

entries.original: Check the boundary: views select saved state; they do not replace its canonical sources. Later machine sessions use new instances, new working memory and newly checked views and permissions.
entries.editorial: Views select saved state while preserving its canonical sources. A new machine session uses a new instance, working memory, checked views and applicable permission.

entries.original: Craft is a software-design Product within the broader Lab. A project can use Craft’s tools; code, models and checks can become Work outputs and evidence. The documentation describes how they fit together without assuming an automatic connector.
entries.editorial: Craft contributes software-design tools within the Lab. Models, code and checks can enter Work as outputs and evidence. Their explanatory fit supplies no automatic operational connector.

entries.original: Check the boundary: a connected ontology node is a representation of a governed subject, not a new authority source. A Craft model edge is not automatically a permitted Lab relation between two Artifact instances.
entries.editorial: A graph node represents a governed subject. Its appearance supplies no new authority, and a Craft edge does not automatically become a permitted Lab instance relation.

entries.original: Check the boundary: Accept is a calculated result. Reserving the available capacity belongs to a separate Operation and requires its own permitted state change. Numeric Calculations remain values, too.
entries.editorial: Accept is a calculated value. Reservation needs a separate Operation and permitted state change. Numeric Calculations also remain derived values.

entries.original: These comparisons explain how to read the model. The reference library retains each exact accepted definition, type contract and connection rule, including its version and boundaries.
entries.editorial: These comparisons help us read the model. The library retains exact accepted meanings, contracts and connection rules with their versions and boundaries.

entries.original: You will prepare a short reading note that identifies a record’s exact identity, selected format, content integrity, standing, scope and claim limits. Have the record, selected contract and applicable registry or decision evidence available. A filename or diagram label cannot supply those facts.
entries.editorial: Start with the record, selected contract and applicable registry or decision evidence. Your reading note should identify exact content, format, integrity, standing, scope and claim limits. A filename or diagram leaves those facts to be checked.

entries.original: This is a manual inspection of the materials. The documentation offers examples and reference contracts; it does not query a live registry.
entries.editorial: These steps inspect saved material manually. The documentation supplies examples and contracts, rather than a live registry query.

entries.original: Open the complete Work example . Record its node_id and schema_version . In the Work reference , select the exact format version and its required fields. Keep the source identity and digest alongside the reading note.
entries.editorial: Open the complete Work example and record node_id and schema_version. Use the Work reference to identify the exact format and required fields. Keep source identity and digest with the note so another reader can recover the same content.

entries.original: A node_id is not necessarily a version field. Use the selected storage/versioning contract to identify the exact content; do not infer version or standing from its spelling.
entries.editorial: node_id does not necessarily identify a version. Follow the selected storage and versioning contract before concluding which content or standing applies.

entries.original: The example says lifecycle_state: candidate and authority_effect: none . No owner acceptance is supplied. Write “candidate documentation specimen” in the note. For real material, check the applicable standing selection and exact owner decision; an admitted Artifact Type does not admit every instance of that type.
entries.editorial: This specimen declares lifecycle_state: candidate and authority_effect: none, with no acceptance evidence. Record it as “candidate documentation specimen.” Real material needs its standing selection and exact owner decision. An accepted type leaves each instance to its own admission route.

entries.original: The reference library presents the standing selected in its captured source material. A source file can retain its authored candidate wording even when a later decision governs its effective standing. Preserve both facts and identify which selection is applicable.
entries.editorial: The library shows standing selected in captured material. A file can keep its authored candidate wording while a later decision establishes effective standing. Save both facts and identify the applicable selection.

entries.original: Check the owner, scope, inputs, outputs, evidence references and claim ceiling (the strongest conclusion its scope and evidence support). Open the referenced material before treating it as support. For each connection, inspect its direction, ordered endpoint kinds and required qualifiers in the declared relation rule. A local relation_refs entry does not contain the complete relation assertion.
entries.editorial: Read owner, scope, inputs, outputs and evidence, then state the strongest supported conclusion. Open the sources before relying on them. For connections, check direction, ordered kinds and qualifiers. A local relation_refs field still needs the complete assertion behind it.

entries.original: For Northstar, Work belongs to the repair Project. It does not authorize deployment, establish a repair or close the incident. The connection examples show the required membership qualifier.
entries.editorial: The Northstar Work belongs to the repair Project. That membership supplies no deployment permission, established repair or incident closure. The connection examples identify the required membership qualifier.

entries.original: Common failures: reading the latest-looking filename as the selected version; treating a schema pass as acceptance; relying on unresolved evidence links; reading a view as a competing authority source.
entries.editorial: A common mistake is treating the latest-looking filename as current. Also check whether a schema pass was mistaken for acceptance, evidence links remain unresolved, or a derived view was treated as another authority source.

entries.original: Prepare a candidate assessment of the omission in the Northstar export. Your output will state what was observed, which material supports it, and what remains unresolved. Use the incident walkthrough for background.
entries.editorial: Prepare a candidate assessment of the Northstar omission. State the observation, its supporting material and unresolved questions. The incident walkthrough supplies the background for this worked example.

entries.original: Have the saved input, output, criterion, method, comparison receipt and applicable authority envelope (the evidence for its scoped permission). Before reading customer material or saving outputs, verify a usable task view and permission for those actions. The steps below use invented local files and a manual preparation route.
entries.editorial: You need saved input and output, criterion, method, comparison receipt and evidence of scoped permission. Before accessing customer material or saving results, check a usable task view and authority for each action. These steps use invented local files and manual preparation.

entries.original: Ask: “Does E12 contain every required identifier from S1 for Northstar with status=active?” Apply the identifier-completeness criterion . Keep snapshot, account, filters and output in the assessment; omitting any of them changes the question.
entries.editorial: The question is whether E12 contains every required identifier from S1 for Northstar with status=active. Use the identifier-completeness criterion and retain snapshot, account, filters and output. Dropping one changes the question.

entries.original: Compare identifiers, then save the exact missing set and the input/output digests. Counts alone cannot show which required rows are absent: an export could have the same number of rows with different identifiers.
entries.editorial: Compare identifiers, then save the exact missing set and input/output digests. Equal counts could hide a different set of rows, so the assessment needs the identifiers behind the counts.

entries.original: The worked receipt lists identifiers 9,801–10,000 as missing. Its digests identify the actual local teaching files. Preserve this datum in the Operational Observation. The selected Measurement Result carrier is specialized for residue entropy; the separate measurement example explains that boundary. No entropy or causal claim follows from the omission count.
entries.editorial: The worked receipt identifies 9,801–10,000 as missing and binds the actual teaching files through digests. Keep that datum in Operational Observation. The selected Measurement Result carrier is specialized for residue entropy, as the separate example explains. The omission count establishes neither entropy nor cause.

entries.original: Open the complete examples for these formats. They include every schema-required field and a one-field failure. For real material, validate the exact selected schema, resolve references and check the ordered relation contracts as separate obligations.
entries.editorial: The complete examples include every required field and a contrasting one-field omission. Real material still needs exact-schema validation, reference closure and ordered connection checks as separate obligations.

entries.original: Package exact record identities, selected versions, evidence digests, the comparison and open questions for the service owner’s review route. The owner can request more evidence or decide a scoped next action. Investigation completion, assessment acceptance, code acceptance, deployment, recovery and incident closure have separate conditions.
entries.editorial: Give the service owner exact identities, versions, evidence digests, comparison and open questions for review. The owner might request further evidence or authorize a scoped next action. Investigation, assessment acceptance, code acceptance, deployment, recovery and closure have separate conditions.

entries.original: Common failures: using counts instead of IDs; losing account or filters; calling a suspected mechanism the cause; saying revision 8 is deployed; calling the incident closed because the proposal was saved.
entries.editorial: Watch for lost account or filters, comparisons of counts alone, a hypothesis stated as cause, or revision 8 called deployed. Saving the proposal leaves incident closure to its own decision.

entries.original: If the task view has expired, prepare a fresh continuation before further agent action. The saved evidence remains inspectable; it does not extend permission or view usability.
entries.editorial: An expired view requires a fresh continuation before further action. Saved evidence stays inspectable while view usability and permission need their own checks.

entries.original: Prepare one exact candidate meaning and the materials its owner needs to review it. Select the applicable Definition contract, semantic owner, authority scope, supporting sources, primary consumers, index/registry route and drift route. The complete criterion specimen uses Definition/v2.
entries.editorial: The owner needs an exact candidate meaning and its review material. Select the Definition contract, semantic owner, scope, sources, consumers, registry/index route and drift route. The complete criterion specimen uses Definition/v2.

entries.original: The specimen passes that selected schema, but its source posture and acceptance obligations remain unresolved. Use it to inspect structure; prepare real source and owner evidence independently.
entries.editorial: That specimen passes the selected schema while source posture and acceptance obligations remain open. It helps examine structure. Real source and owner evidence still have to be prepared.

entries.original: Identify the term, stable identity and proposed version. State one governing (normative) meaning, its applicability, exclusions and boundaries. For export identifier completeness, declare S, A, F and E, then require every identifier in RequiredIds(S,A,F) to appear in ExportedIds(E).
entries.editorial: Name the term, stable identity and proposed version. State the governing meaning with applicability, exclusions and boundaries. For identifier coverage, declare S, A, F and E, requiring every RequiredIds(S,A,F) identifier in ExportedIds(E).

entries.original: Value accuracy, live-source consistency, access permission and incident recovery each fall outside that criterion. A case with all IDs present but incorrect values exposes this boundary. It does not falsify the identifier-coverage statement.
entries.editorial: Value accuracy, live-source consistency, access permission and recovery are outside this criterion. An export with all IDs and incorrect values exposes that boundary while still satisfying identifier coverage.

entries.original: The scientific/formal voice states the governing meaning. The plain-language and domain-context voices are explicitly non-normative explanations. Use the same scope in each voice. Avoid making “every customer record everywhere” the plain-language explanation of a statement about one fixed account, filter set and snapshot.
entries.editorial: The scientific/formal voice governs meaning. Plain-language and domain-context voices explain it without expanding its scope. “Every customer record everywhere” would be a different claim from one fixed account, filters and snapshot.

entries.original: Declare testable conditions and notation. Preserve an example that satisfies the criterion and an example that fails it, with the selected inputs visible.
entries.editorial: Make conditions and notation testable. Keep a satisfying example and a failing example with their selected inputs visible to the reviewer.

entries.original: Schema checks establish required representation. Reference closure, source posture, generated projection consistency, the registry/index and semantic review remain separate checks.
entries.editorial: A schema pass covers representation. Reference closure, source posture, generated-view consistency, registry/index and semantic review still need separate checks.

entries.original: Submit the exact candidate version with the formal meaning, explanatory voices, boundaries, source evidence, affected consumers, proposed index/registry changes and review findings. Keep open obligations visible. Only the applicable exact owner decision can make that version governing authority within its declared scope.
entries.editorial: Submit the exact version, formal meaning, explanations, boundaries, source evidence, affected consumers, proposed registry/index changes and findings. Keep open obligations visible. Authority for that version and scope comes only from the applicable exact owner decision.

entries.original: Common failures: treating a schema pass as acceptance; hiding changed meaning as a formatting update; allowing the plain-language voice to expand the formal scope; inferring agent permission from definition acceptance.
entries.editorial: Review for acceptance inferred from structure, changed meaning disguised as formatting, explanations exceeding formal scope, and agent permission inferred from definition acceptance.

entries.original: A changed meaning needs its applicable semantic change route. After acceptance, update affected consumers and derived views through their own rules. Read the lifecycle distinctions →
entries.editorial: A changed meaning follows its semantic route. Accepted changes also need affected consumers and derived views updated under their own rules. The lifecycle distinctions explain those routes.

entries.original: Prepare a usable continuation for an interrupted investigation. You need the saved Project State, exact assignment, current authority evidence, applicable policies, view request and selected freshness/expiry rules. Recovery of project knowledge and permission to act must both be checked.
entries.editorial: Recovering knowledge is part of continuation. So is current permission. Bring saved Project State, exact assignment, authority evidence, policies, view request and freshness rules before resuming an interrupted investigation.

entries.original: At 10:10 UTC, Northstar task view 3 expires. The 09:45–10:15 delegation may still be current, but the expired view prevents continued reliance on that task context.
entries.editorial: Northstar view 3 expires at 10:10 UTC. Its 09:45–10:15 delegation might still be current. The expired information nevertheless prevents continued reliance on that context.

entries.original: Record why the view is unusable and where the agent stopped. Persist only outputs permitted by the recording route, preserving their candidate standing and source references. Do not use temporary session notes as an accepted project conclusion.
entries.editorial: Record the unusable view and stopping point. Save only permitted outputs, preserving candidate standing and source references. Temporary notes leave project conclusions to the applicable recording and acceptance route.

entries.original: If the same session remains active, refreshing its views does not itself renew or expand authority. If the session terminates, its machine instance and short memory end with it.
entries.editorial: Refreshing an active session’s views leaves its authority unchanged. If the session ends, the machine instance and working memory end too.

entries.original: For a later session, select saved Project State: Work, comparison receipt, observations, assessment material, decisions and unresolved questions. Generate or obtain newly checked Context and Ontology Views under their applicable request, selection and freshness contracts.
entries.editorial: For a later session, select saved Work, comparison, observations, assessment material, decisions and open questions. Obtain newly checked Context and Ontology Views under the applicable request, selection and freshness contracts.

entries.original: The Context View example identifies included material by selector and digest, records exclusions and sets expiry. A structurally valid JSON view can still be unusable because its source or time conditions changed.
entries.editorial: The view specimen identifies included material by selector and digest, states exclusions and expires. Valid JSON can still be unusable when sources or time conditions change.

entries.original: Read the exact current assignment and delegation separately. Check eligible agent, scope, action kinds, policies, approval gates, period, revocation and budgets. At or after 10:15 UTC the old delegation cannot support later actions. A new session may need a new or renewed grant; copying the old context does not transfer permission.
entries.editorial: Read the current assignment and delegation separately. Check agent eligibility, scope, actions, policies, gates, period, revocation and budgets. At or after 10:15 UTC, the old grant supports no later action. A new session needs its applicable grant. Copying context transfers no permission.

entries.original: Assignment describes expected participation. Delegation supplies its scoped grant only when its governing evidence is established. Neither a view nor an agent’s recollection grants authority.
entries.editorial: Assignment records participation. Delegation supplies a scoped grant only with its governing evidence established. Views and recollection supply no independent authority.

entries.original: Create the applicable session envelope for the selected concrete instance, assignment, exact views, policies, authority, inputs, budgets and cursor. For a new session, use a new ephemeral machine instance and session-owned working memory. The Agent Session specimen shows the required fields.
entries.editorial: Prepare the session envelope with its instance, assignment, exact views, policies, authority, inputs, budgets and cursor. A new session needs a new ephemeral machine instance and its own working memory. The specimen shows required fields.

entries.original: Stop again if permission is revoked or expires, a view becomes unusable, the budget is exhausted or an approval gate is reached. Preserve the previous session’s records as history; do not silently resume its temporary memory.
entries.editorial: Pause again for expired or revoked permission, unusable views, exhausted budget or approval gates. Earlier session records stay as history. Its temporary memory is unavailable for silent resumption.

entries.original: Common failures: resuming on the expired view; treating saved state as permission; giving a machine instance durable private memory; calling an assessment accepted because it survived a session.
entries.editorial: Common mistakes are treating an expired view as current, saved state as permission, a machine instance as durable private memory, or a surviving candidate assessment as accepted.

entries.original: These are complete documentation specimens against the selected record schemas. Their invented example: identities have no registry standing. Passing a schema checks representation; it does not accept a record, establish its claims or grant permission. The links open local JSON files.
entries.editorial: These complete specimens use the selected schemas and invented example: identities with no registry standing. Structural validation leaves acceptance, claim support and permission to their own records. The links open local JSON.

entries.original: The saved input S1 , output E12 and comparison receipt reproduce the fixed Northstar example: 10,000 required identifiers, 9,800 exported and 200 confirmed missing.
entries.editorial: S1, E12 and the comparison receipt reproduce the fixed case: 10,000 required identifiers, 9,800 exported and 200 confirmed missing.

entries.original: The fields describe the proposed permission envelope. This candidate JSON does not issue a real grant. Verify the delegator’s authority and the exact decision before acting.
entries.editorial: The candidate describes a permission envelope, without issuing a real grant. Check the delegator’s authority and exact decision before acting.

entries.original: The specimen expires at 10:10 UTC. It still passes the schema after that time, but the agent cannot rely on it as a usable task view.
entries.editorial: This view expires at 10:10 UTC. Its schema can still validate afterward while the task information is unusable.

entries.original: The selected carrier is specialized for residue entropy although the semantic definition is broader. This separate toy model has five equally likely states: H = log₂(5) ≈ 2.322 bits. It supplies no Northstar incident evidence. The incident count belongs in its saved comparison and observation.
entries.editorial: The selected carrier is specifically for residue entropy, despite the broader semantic meaning. The separate toy model has five equally likely states, H = log₂(5) ≈ 2.322 bits. It contributes no Northstar evidence. Save the incident count in its comparison and observation.

entries.original: The criterion binds snapshot, account, filters and output. Source posture, index synchronization and owner acceptance still require review. The all-zero generator digest explicitly marks an unresolved binding: replace it with the actual selected Definition generator’s digest before relying on that binding. Correct values are outside the identifier-coverage criterion.
entries.editorial: The criterion binds snapshot, account, filters and output. Source posture, index synchronization and acceptance still need review. The all-zero generator digest marks an unresolved binding and must be replaced with the actual selected Definition generator digest before reliance. Correct values are outside identifier coverage.

entries.original: A record’s local connection reference is not the complete relation assertion. The ordered endpoint kinds and required qualifiers below come from the selected relation rule. These patterns convey no permission.
entries.editorial: A local connection reference still needs its complete assertion. The patterns below take ordered kinds and qualifiers from the selected rule. They supply no permission.

entries.original: Suppose every required identifier appears in the export, but several email addresses have incorrect values. The identifier-coverage definition is satisfied; it says nothing about value accuracy. This is a boundary of the claim, not a malformed record.
entries.editorial: Suppose the required identifiers are all present while several email values are wrong. Identifier coverage is satisfied; value accuracy still needs its own criterion. The example exposes a claim boundary rather than a malformed record.

entries.original: How an agent might improve a robot's movement code, choose better experiments and learn from physical trials.
entries.editorial: Follow a proposed investigation into robot movement code, better experiment choices and learning from physical trials.

entries.original: A hypothetical warehouse arm provides the running example. The essays propose an application of the Lab; research references support the individual mechanisms discussed.
entries.editorial: The warehouse arm is hypothetical. This series proposes an application of the Lab, with research references supporting the mechanisms discussed.

entries.original: The agent investigates both the robot's movement and the method used to improve it. Each session continues from the evidence left by earlier work.
entries.editorial: The agent examines the movement and its own method for improving it. Each session starts from evidence earlier work has left behind.

entries.original: A warehouse robot brings a package to a packing station. As its arm approaches the target, it overshoots, corrects, then corrects again. Eventually the package settles. The routine works often enough to remain in service, but the last part of the movement wastes time and behaves differently with different loads. An agent is asked to improve it.
entries.editorial: A warehouse arm brings a package to a packing station. Near the target, it overshoots and corrects several times before settling. The routine often works, yet the final movement takes time and responds differently to changing loads. An agent is asked to improve it.

entries.original: The agent could slow the final approach, alter the trajectory or adjust the controller. Choosing among them requires knowing what the current program does, which physical assumptions it makes and what counts as a successful placement. That information may be scattered across earlier code, experiments and decisions.
entries.editorial: The agent could slow the approach, change the trajectory or adjust the controller. Choosing a response needs the current program, physical assumptions and a criterion for successful placement. Earlier code, experiments and decisions might hold different parts of that account.

entries.original: CyberAlchemy Lab could bring those pieces together. This series follows a hypothetical investigation into the robot's movement routine, with research references supplying precedents for particular mechanisms. It proposes an application of the Lab around one question: how could an agent use an explicit development history to make its next decision better informed?
entries.editorial: The Lab could connect those parts. This hypothetical investigation asks whether an explicit development history helps an agent make a better-informed next decision. The research references supply precedents for particular mechanisms, with the proposed integration still needing evaluation.

entries.original: Before changing the code, the agent needs to understand the task. A package must arrive at the assigned position and orientation, within a stated tolerance, and remain there long enough for placement to be confirmed. A motion that passes through the target and immediately moves away has a different outcome. Completion time matters once the placement conditions have been met.
entries.editorial: Before editing code, establish the task. The package must reach its assigned position and orientation within tolerance and remain there long enough to confirm placement. Passing through the target and moving away would be a different outcome. Completion time matters after those conditions are met.

entries.original: A definition gives successful placement a precise meaning. A contract specifies the information needed to describe an assignment and report its outcome. An experiment records whether a particular routine satisfied those conditions. The agent can compare two programs against the same task.
entries.editorial: A definition states successful placement. A contract governs assignment and outcome information. An experiment records whether a particular routine meets the conditions. Two programs can then be assessed against the same task.

entries.original: If the candidate reports success as soon as it crosses the target, it may appear faster simply because it stops measuring too early. The task definition lets the agent detect that error, provided the evaluator implements the rule correctly. Changing an admitted definition would change the obligations of dependent routines and evaluators. Such a revision needs an explicit decision about its scope.
entries.editorial: A candidate reporting success as it crosses the target might look faster because measurement stops too soon. The definition exposes that error if the evaluator implements it correctly. Revising an admitted definition changes dependent obligations and needs an explicit scope decision.

entries.original: An ontology view could connect the placement requirement to its motion routine, implementation and experiments performed with a particular robot model. These connections help the agent find relevant evidence. A predictive world model serves a different purpose: it estimates what will happen when the robot acts.
entries.editorial: An Ontology View could connect placement requirements, movement code, implementations and experiments for the robot model. Those connections help retrieve evidence. A predictive world model has a different job: estimating what happens after an action.

entries.original: For the oscillating arm, that model might combine rigid-body dynamics with estimates of payload, friction and actuator delay. At a chosen time step, its prediction can be written as x_next = F(x, u, theta, e): the next state depends on the current state x, command u, parameters theta and environmental conditions e. A different payload estimate can change the prediction for the same command.
entries.editorial: The arm’s predictive model might combine rigid-body dynamics with payload, friction and delay estimates. At a selected time step, x_next = F(x, u, theta, e) relates next state to current state x, command u, parameters theta and environment e. A changed payload estimate can change the same command’s prediction.

entries.original: Physics constrains the possibilities the agent considers. Mass and inertia affect acceleration; actuator limits restrict the available commands; contact changes how forces are transmitted. MuJoCo provides a concrete example of a simulator that represents dynamics, actuation and constraints. Its predictions depend on the model and numerical configuration supplied to it. MuJoCo computation documentation
entries.editorial: Physics constrains the candidate. Mass and inertia affect acceleration, actuator limits restrict commands, and contact affects forces. MuJoCo illustrates simulation of dynamics, actuation and constraints. Its predictions depend on the supplied model and numerical configuration.

entries.original: The agent can use simulation to investigate a slower final approach before proposing a physical trial. It can compare trajectories and examine where the candidate becomes sensitive to payload changes. A learned component might eventually help account for discrepancies that the physics model leaves unresolved. Its training data and supported conditions would also become part of the model's history.
entries.editorial: The agent could examine a slower approach in simulation before proposing a physical trial. Trajectories and payload sensitivity give it a basis for comparison. A learned component might help with remaining model discrepancies, with its training data and supported conditions recorded too.

entries.original: DreamerV3 provides a research precedent for learning an environment model and improving behavior through imagined trajectories. Our proposed application asks how to connect such predictions to the exact movement program, task requirements and development evidence. That integration would need its own evaluation. DreamerV3 paper
entries.editorial: DreamerV3 supplies a precedent for learned environment models and behavior improvement through imagined trajectories. Connecting those predictions to this exact program, task and development evidence would require its own investigation.

entries.original: With a candidate approach in mind, the agent describes the intended behavior: reduce speed during the final approach and confirm that the package has settled before reporting completion. The description identifies frames, units, required observations and responses to missing observations. It gives the code generator something specific to implement and the evaluator something to examine.
entries.editorial: The candidate description now has a job: slow the final approach and confirm settling before reporting completion. It needs frames, units, observations and responses to missing observations. Those details give generation and evaluation an explicit subject.

entries.original: Some obligations can be formalized. A command-limiting routine might be required to satisfy abs(u_i) <= limit_i for every actuator channel in its input domain. A proof would establish that property under its formal assumptions. Successful placement and obstacle clearance require further arguments, as does the correspondence between the mathematical routine, compiled program and robot interface.
entries.editorial: Some obligations admit formal treatment. A command limiter might require abs(u_i) <= limit_i for every channel within its input domain. A proof establishes that property under its assumptions. Placement, clearance and correspondence with compiled code and the robot interface still need further arguments.

entries.original: The agent then compares the candidate with a fixed baseline under the same declared initial conditions. Variations in package properties and model parameters probe the intended operating range. Placement success remains the primary task condition; settling time, overshoot, command violations and computational cost describe the change more closely. Cases used for tuning are kept distinct from cases reserved for evaluation.
entries.editorial: Compare the candidate with a fixed baseline under the same declared initial conditions. Vary package properties and model parameters within the intended range. Placement remains the primary condition; settling time, overshoot, violations and computational cost describe the result more closely. Keep tuning and evaluation cases separate.

entries.original: Governance helps the agent decide what the results allow it to do next. Authority identifies governing definitions, contracts and permissions, including permitted experiments. Provenance traces a result to the code and model configuration that produced it. Lifecycle distinguishes proposed, evaluated and adopted implementations within their scope. An assignment to improve the robot must be accompanied by authority for the intended effects.
entries.editorial: The governance records bound the next action. Authority identifies definitions, contracts and experimental permissions. Provenance traces results to code and configuration. Lifecycle distinguishes proposals, evaluations and adoption. The assignment to improve movement still needs authority for its intended effects.

entries.original: The investigation can outlast the session that began it. The Machine Agent is ephemeral; its short-term memory belongs to the session. Durable Project State provides long-term continuity through context and ontology views that select the relevant code, evidence and decisions. A successor can recover what was attempted and why a candidate was retained or set aside.
entries.editorial: The investigation can continue after its first session ends. The machine agent and working memory are temporary. Project State preserves code, evidence and decisions, selected through current Context and Ontology Views. A successor can recover attempts and reasons for retaining or rejecting candidates.

entries.original: Suppose the slower approach reduces oscillation with the familiar package but loses that advantage when the load changes. The agent now has a narrower question: what explains the sensitivity, and which experiment would distinguish the likely causes? The quality of that experiment will determine how much the next code change teaches it.
entries.editorial: Suppose the slower approach helps with a familiar package and loses its advantage under a heavier load. The next question becomes what explains that sensitivity and which experiment could distinguish causes. That choice affects what the next code revision teaches the investigation.

entries.original: The first candidate improves the robot's final approach for one package and struggles with a heavier one. An agent could respond by generating another controller. It could also spend its next experiment finding out why the improvement failed to carry over. The second choice may save considerable work, provided the experiment can separate plausible explanations.
entries.editorial: The agent could generate another controller. It could instead investigate why the first improvement failed to transfer to the heavier package. The second approach might save work if the experiment separates plausible explanations.

entries.original: The agent is developing both a movement routine and a method for investigating such routines. Over several tasks, it might learn when to inspect an interface, recalibrate a model or change the controller. CyberAlchemy Lab could preserve the evidence needed to assess whether those habits make development more effective.
entries.editorial: Now there are two things to improve: movement and the method for examining movement. Across tasks, the agent might learn when to inspect an interface, recalibrate a model or change a controller. The Lab could retain evidence about whether those habits improve development.

entries.original: Consider three explanations for the heavier package's oscillation. The movement plan may rely on a payload estimate appropriate to the lighter package. The controller may respond poorly even with an accurate estimate. Or a conversion at the command interface may change the intended command. All three could produce a similar trace at the target. Naming a failure mode helps organize the investigation; establishing its cause requires evidence.
entries.editorial: Three explanations could fit the oscillation: the wrong payload estimate, poor controller response despite an accurate estimate, or an interface conversion changing the command. Similar traces can have different causes. A failure-mode label organizes the question while evidence establishes the explanation.

entries.original: The experiment's recorded connections lead back to the model assumptions, command contract and source revision. Provenance identifies what ran; lifecycle helps establish whether earlier findings concern the current configuration. A unit-conversion defect in a retired interface may suggest a check, but the current interface needs examination on its own terms.
entries.editorial: The experiment points back to assumptions, command contract and source revision. Provenance identifies what ran; lifecycle helps assess whether older findings still concern this configuration. A retired interface defect suggests a check, with the current interface needing its own examination.

entries.original: For the payload hypothesis, the agent could inspect the estimate used to plan the movement and compare runs with corrected estimates. Varying the simulated load would characterize sensitivity within the model; physical calibration would need observations of the actual load. For the interface hypothesis, it could compare requested commands with values received after conversion. The investigations reveal different things and have different costs.
entries.editorial: For payload, inspect the planning estimate and compare corrected estimates. Simulation characterizes sensitivity within the model; physical calibration needs load observations. For the interface, compare requested and received commands after conversion. Each investigation has different information and cost.

entries.original: An experiment should reduce a particular uncertainty. Hundreds of controller variants may improve a score while leaving its cause obscure. Comparing competing explanations gives the agent a stronger basis for a change. Where factors interact, the design must account for those interactions; changing one variable at a time is only one option.
entries.editorial: Choose the uncertainty the experiment should reduce. Many controller variants could improve a score without explaining the result. Comparing causes gives a stronger basis for change. Interacting factors need a design accounting for their interaction; one-variable-at-a-time work is only one option.

entries.original: Formal reasoning can sharpen the diagnosis. An independent requirement might specify the command range and input domain. Lean's proof-validation guidance emphasizes both proof validity and the meaning of the statement proved. The agent needs to examine assumptions and open obligations, especially when code and proofs are generated within the same development process. Lean proof-validation reference
entries.editorial: Formal reasoning can sharpen that question. An independent requirement might specify range and input domain. Lean’s guidance distinguishes valid proofs from the meaning of their statements. Generated code and proofs still need scrutiny of assumptions and open obligations.

entries.original: Imagine that the routine limits each command correctly, yet the package still oscillates. A proof of that routine would settle a narrow question about command magnitude while leaving stability and settling behavior open. The agent can use the result to refine the investigation, preserving the proof's actual scope.
entries.editorial: Suppose the limiter meets its property while the package oscillates. The proof settles a narrow command-magnitude question. Stability and settling remain open, giving the agent a more precise next investigation.

entries.original: Code generation fits within this experimental structure. The agent might propose two terminal timing rules and compare their outcomes. In reinforcement learning, it could generate a reward program used to train a controller. Eureka demonstrates an LLM generating reward code and revising it through evaluation feedback. Assessing direct movement-code generation would require a separate investigation. Eureka project
entries.editorial: Generation belongs in that experimental process. The agent could compare terminal timing rules or generate reinforcement-learning reward code. Eureka demonstrates reward generation with feedback-based revision. Direct movement-code generation would need separate evidence.

entries.original: A training reward and task success also need distinct meanings. Rewarding proximity to the target may overlook whether the package stays there. The placement definition remains the reference for evaluation. A proposed change to that definition or the evaluator needs its own justification and adoption through the appropriate authority.
entries.editorial: A training reward also needs a boundary. Proximity alone might reward arrival without settling. The placement definition supplies evaluation’s criterion. Changing that definition or evaluator needs justification and the applicable adoption decision.

entries.original: Suppose the investigation finds a frame-conversion error that earlier tuning had obscured. An operational lesson could recommend checking requested and received commands before retuning this interface. Its record would identify supporting evidence, affected configurations and conditions for reuse. It would also specify contrary evidence, such as comparable investigations where the check adds cost without improving diagnosis.
entries.editorial: Suppose the investigation identifies a frame-conversion defect hidden by earlier tuning. A lesson could recommend checking requested and received commands before retuning that interface. Its evidence, affected configurations and reuse conditions should be explicit. Comparable cases where the check costs more without improving diagnosis would count against its predicted benefit.

entries.original: Classification makes the lesson easier to find. The symptom might be filed under terminal oscillation, the confirmed failure mode under frame conversion, and the lesson under interface diagnosis. Those categories provide different routes to the same evidence. A future agent searching for an oscillating placement can find the case without assuming that every oscillation has the same cause.
entries.editorial: Classification helps a future agent find the case by symptom, confirmed mode or lesson purpose. Terminal oscillation, frame conversion and interface diagnosis answer different questions. Finding this case should still leave the cause of a new oscillation to investigation.

entries.original: To assess that lesson beyond one case, the agent could compare the diagnostic sequence with the previous workflow on other tasks under similar budgets. Measures include time to diagnosis, experiments consumed and regressions missed. Tasks withheld from the process's development would help reveal whether the method transfers beyond the cases that suggested it.
entries.editorial: Assess the proposed method on other tasks against the earlier workflow under comparable budgets. Diagnosis time, experiments used and missed regressions provide useful observations. Hold-out tasks examine transfer beyond the cases that produced the idea.

entries.original: A reflection written after a session supplies a hypothesis about the method's value. Comparative evidence would support adopting it: better diagnoses or candidates, with an acceptable use of time and computation.
entries.editorial: A session’s reflection proposes value in the method. Comparative evidence would support adoption through better diagnoses or candidates within acceptable time and computation.

entries.original: Saving an evaluated lesson changes what a later session can retrieve and use; it does not by itself update a language model's weights. Durable learning may also appear in revised code, calibrated physics parameters or a trained controller. The session's temporary reasoning expires. Project State supplies the persistent record, selected through context and ontology views for the next task.
entries.editorial: A saved evaluated lesson changes what another session can retrieve. It does not itself change language-model weights. Revised code, calibrated physics or trained controllers can also retain learning. Temporary session reasoning ends, while Project State supplies the record for newly selected views.

entries.original: Two connected feedback loops emerge. One changes movement in response to measured behavior. The other changes how the agent diagnoses problems and chooses experiments. The second loop may prevent repeated mistakes or introduce procedures whose costs outweigh their benefits. The record must allow either result to be recognized.
entries.editorial: One feedback loop changes movement from measured behavior. Another changes diagnosis and experiment selection. The second might prevent mistakes or introduce procedures whose costs exceed their benefits. The record needs to support either conclusion.

entries.original: A candidate that eventually meets its formal and simulation criteria gives the agent a reason to prepare a physical trial. The development history explains its selection and identifies uncertain assumptions. Those assumptions indicate which observations may be most informative when the routine meets the robot.
entries.editorial: A candidate meeting formal and simulation criteria can support preparing a physical trial. The history explains its selection and uncertain assumptions. Those assumptions help choose informative observations on the robot.

entries.original: The investigation returns to the packing station. In simulation, the candidate routine settles more smoothly across the selected package conditions. Some code properties have also been proved under explicit assumptions. The agent now needs to compare its predictions with measurements from an authorized trial on the warehouse arm.
entries.editorial: We return to the packing station in the proposed case. The candidate settles more smoothly in selected simulations, and some code properties have proofs under assumptions. An authorized physical trial would examine those predictions on the warehouse arm.

entries.original: The simulator predicts how the arm should respond; the robot supplies measurements from a physical trial. Differences can teach the agent about the code, the model or their connection, provided the investigation preserves enough information to distinguish the explanations.
entries.editorial: The simulator predicts; the robot supplies measurements. A discrepancy can concern code, model or correspondence between them. The investigation needs enough information to distinguish those explanations.

entries.original: The candidate's implementation package identifies the source revision, executable build, configuration, interface contract and supporting evidence. Authorization specifies the robot, task and conditions for the trial. The agent needs to establish both its technical ability to send a command and its permission to produce the intended physical effect.
entries.editorial: The implementation package identifies source, build, configuration, interface and evidence. Trial authorization states robot, task and conditions. The agent needs technical command ability and permission for the physical effect.

entries.original: Movement depends on a chain of interpretations. A request becomes a target in a declared coordinate frame. The program produces a reference trajectory; the controller converts tracking error into actuator commands; the interface delivers them at the required rate. Sensors supply placement observations. Incorrect units, timing or calibration at any connection can change the behavior.
entries.editorial: A movement passes through several interpretations: target and frame, trajectory, controller error, actuator commands, timed interface delivery and sensor observations. Units, timing or calibration errors at a connection can change the result.

entries.original: The agent needs evidence that the evaluated code corresponds to the program used in the trial and that its interface bindings are correct. A trajectory must reach the controller in the expected frame. Assumed delay must be compared with observed timing. The Lab could make these correspondences explicit enough to inspect after an unexpected result.
entries.editorial: We need evidence connecting evaluated code to the trial program and its interfaces. The trajectory must use the expected frame; observed timing must be compared with assumed delay. The Lab could make those correspondences recoverable after an unexpected result.

entries.original: The deliberating agent and motion controller work at different timescales. The controller executes the adopted implementation at the required rate. Between experiments, the agent examines results and prepares changes, while the robot can continue using its known implementation. An adaptive controller could update within a declared operating envelope; extending that envelope requires a further decision.
entries.editorial: Agent deliberation and control use different timescales. The controller runs the adopted implementation at its required rate. Between trials, an agent assesses results and prepares changes. An adaptive controller might update within a declared envelope, with expansion requiring another decision.

entries.original: The physical package may have a different mass distribution, the grip may introduce contact effects, or execution delays may vary. Evaluating across simulation parameters can help investigate these differences. The range needs physical justification: its usefulness depends on covering conditions relevant to the robot.
entries.editorial: Physical mass distribution, grip contact and delay can differ from simulation. Parameter variation helps investigate those gaps, provided the range has physical justification for this robot.

entries.original: DrEureka provides a research example of language models helping construct reward functions and simulation parameter distributions for transfer to physical robots. Applying a similar method to our arm would require evidence for this hardware and task, including the simulator's adequacy and the chosen parameter ranges. DrEureka project
entries.editorial: DrEureka studies language-model assistance with rewards and simulation parameter distributions for transfer to robots. Applying similar methods to this arm needs hardware- and task-specific evidence about simulation adequacy and chosen ranges.

entries.original: Suppose the trial produces more oscillation than predicted. The record includes position traces, commands, timing and placement outcomes, tied to the exact implementation. Before diagnosing the discrepancy, the agent assesses measurement quality. Missing observations or uncertain clock alignment may prevent a useful comparison with the prediction.
entries.editorial: Suppose the trial oscillates more than predicted. Save position traces, commands, timing and outcomes against the exact implementation. Then examine measurement quality. Missing observations or uncertain clock alignment could prevent a useful comparison.

entries.original: If a command arrives later than assumed, the agent can examine how delay affects predicted movement. If timing agrees, payload calibration or contact behavior may deserve attention. Further observations, parameter changes or code revisions follow the evidence, with alternative explanations retained until the investigation can distinguish them.
