entries.editorial: If delivery is late, investigate delay in the predicted dynamics. If timing agrees, examine payload or contact. Additional observations, parameter changes and code revisions follow evidence, with competing explanations retained until distinguishable.

entries.original: A revised world model changes the basis for code evaluation. Earlier evidence remains in the history, but its applicability needs reconsideration. The ontology helps the agent find experiments and candidates that depended on the changed assumption, then choose which comparisons to repeat.
entries.editorial: A revised world model changes the basis for evaluation. Earlier evidence stays in history while applicability is reconsidered. Ontology connections help locate dependent experiments and candidates and choose which comparisons to repeat.

entries.original: Physical effects can also become uncertain. A command may execute before a connection fails, leaving placement unconfirmed. Repeating it could act on a package that has already moved. The agent first uses an applicable observation procedure to reconcile physical state. The issued-command record supports recovery, but cannot establish the package's location by itself.
entries.editorial: A command can execute before its connection fails, leaving placement uncertain. Repetition could move a package already moved. First reconcile physical state through the applicable observation procedure. The issued-command record supports recovery while leaving location to observation.

entries.original: Governance answers practical questions here. Authority identifies what governs placement and who may change or execute the routine within scope. Provenance traces observations to their implementations. Lifecycle identifies proposals, evaluated candidates and adopted or superseded records. The agent uses these distinctions to determine which evidence applies and which next actions are permitted.
entries.editorial: Authority establishes placement meanings and scoped permissions for changes or execution. Provenance identifies observation inputs and implementations. Lifecycle distinguishes proposals, evaluations, adoption and supersession. The agent uses those records to decide which evidence and next actions apply.

entries.original: A routine may be adopted for one package class while another remains under investigation. Evidence can support extending that scope, reveal a regression or justify withdrawing a candidate. The agent prepares the proposed change; the decision follows the required authority, including limits on its delegation.
entries.editorial: Adoption might cover one package class while another stays under investigation. Evidence can support scope expansion, expose regression or justify withdrawal. The agent prepares a proposal; the decision follows its required authority and delegation limits.

entries.original: A later session reconstructs this position from Project State. Context and ontology views select the applicable implementation, unresolved discrepancies and lessons. The Machine Agent remains ephemeral, with short-term memory attached to its session. Continuity depends on records that another session can examine and use.
entries.editorial: A later session recovers that position from Project State through views selecting implementation, discrepancies and lessons. The machine agent is ephemeral, with working memory belonging to its session. Continuity comes from examinable records.

entries.original: Physical experience can improve the experimental method too. If execution delay repeatedly explains problems missed in simulation, the agent could propose using measured delay variation in future evaluations. It would assess whether this detects problems earlier and improves the candidates reaching physical trials.
entries.editorial: Trials can improve the method too. If measured delay keeps explaining failures missed in simulation, the agent could propose delay variation in future evaluations. It would then assess earlier detection and the quality of candidates reaching trials.

entries.original: Maintaining this history also consumes time, computation and storage. An empirical evaluation should examine completion, constraint violations, recovery and regressions alongside those costs. The architecture earns its place if the preserved information helps agents make better decisions under comparable conditions.
entries.editorial: Keeping this history costs time, computation and storage. An empirical study should compare those costs with completion, violations, recovery and regressions. Preserved information needs to improve decisions under comparable conditions to justify the architecture.

entries.original: The next unfamiliar package gives that proposition a concrete test. A new session could locate the routine's adopted conditions, inspect its payload assumptions and retrieve an experiment that previously distinguished causes of oscillation. Further code changes and measurements may be needed. The useful continuity is an examined history from which to begin, and a clearer account to leave of what the robot can do.
entries.editorial: The next unfamiliar package offers a test. A new agent can find adopted conditions, payload assumptions and earlier experiments separating causes of oscillation. More code changes and measurements might follow. The history supplies a basis for beginning and a clearer account to leave for the next session.

entries.original: Inspect definitions, required record formats and permitted connections. Acceptance status and version labels are shown separately. Expanded essays and research are available below.
entries.editorial: Read the definitions, formats and permitted connections behind the model. Version labels and recorded acceptance appear separately, with essays and research available below.

entries.original: CyberAlchemy Lab organizes project work through explicit meanings, record requirements, evidence and decisions. The expanded essays explain the model. The catalog lets you inspect the definitions and contracts behind it.
entries.editorial: The Lab organizes work through meanings, record requirements, evidence and decisions. The essays explain the connections. This catalog gives you the exact records behind that explanation.

entries.original: New to the model? Follow an incident to see what the agent reads and records at each step. Compare the concepts when similar terms are hard to distinguish.
entries.editorial: If you’re new to the model, follow the incident first. It shows what the agent reads and records. The concept comparisons help when similar names obscure different responsibilities.

entries.original: For a first reading, start with Authority begins with meaning , then What the Lab organizes and An agent’s working session . For the implementation status in this source snapshot, read What is operational today .
entries.editorial: Begin with Authority begins with meaning, then What the Lab organizes and An agent’s working session. What is operational today describes the implementation evidence in this captured snapshot.

entries.original: Accepted means a recorded decision has admitted that exact definition or contract for its stated scope. Selected current means the inspected registry uses it in its current selection. Neither status establishes deployment, activation or successful use.
entries.editorial: Accepted means a decision admitted an exact version within scope. Selected current means the inspected registry includes it in its current selection. Deployment, activation and successful use still need their own evidence.

entries.original: An identity distinguishes one definition or contract from another. A version identifies a particular revision. Matching display names do not make two records identical. Three definition names appear in both Lab and Craft workflow scopes; their labels identify which entry you are reading.
entries.editorial: Identity distinguishes records; version identifies a revision. Equal display names leave identity to be checked. Three definition names appear in both Lab and Craft workflow scopes, with labels identifying the entry you’re reading.

entries.original: An accepted record can retain an older version name containing “candidate.” Its recorded acceptance determines its standing. Earlier accepted versions remain in the historical lists even when the current selection uses another version.
entries.editorial: An accepted version might still have “candidate” in its older name. Its recorded acceptance governs standing. Earlier accepted versions remain in history when selection moves to a successor.

entries.original: A type contract can be accepted while an instance using it is still proposed. A status field in the schema describes the record form it validates; it is not the type registry’s acceptance decision. Each instance retains its own standing.
entries.editorial: A type can be accepted while an instance is proposed. A schema’s status field describes validated record structure. The type registry’s decision and each instance’s standing remain separate.

entries.original: This library describes the sources captured on 8 October 2026 . Its counts cover the selected registries, not every repository object or every implemented feature. Short introductions and essays explain the records; they do not change their authority. The exact governing statements and original source links remain available in each entry.
entries.editorial: The catalog retains sources captured on 8 October 2026. Its totals concern selected registries, rather than all files or features. Introductions and essays explain those records while leaving authority to its governing selection. Each entry retains exact statements and source links.

entries.original: Project State can preserve or reference proposals, evidence and unresolved matters with their own statuses. Acceptance of that state does not automatically accept every included record or promote its sources.
entries.editorial: Project State can keep proposals, evidence and unresolved matters with their own status. Accepting the state supplies no automatic acceptance for every included record or source.

entries.original: Names such as source_ref are exact field keys, retained so the explanation can be checked against the schema. A key ending in _ref refers to another record; _version_ref selects an exact version. Read the schema to learn which reference kinds are permitted.
entries.editorial: Keys such as source_ref stay exact so you can compare the explanation with the schema. _ref points to another record, and _version_ref selects an exact revision. The schema identifies permitted reference kinds.

entries.original: In a JSON schema, required names mandatory fields, properties describes fields, enum restricts a value to a listed set, and $ref points to another schema section. A discriminator is the field-and-value rule that identifies a record’s type. These clues help you navigate; the full schema and type contract supply the complete requirements.
entries.editorial: In JSON schema, required lists mandatory fields, properties describes them, enum restricts alternatives and $ref points to a schema section. A discriminator identifies type through a field and value. These are reading clues. The complete contract and schema govern the requirements.

entries.original: The business examples illustrate the model. The essays distinguish accepted definitions and contracts from implemented software, recorded past executions and proposed work. This explanation does not itself approve changes or authorize actions.
entries.editorial: The business cases illustrate the model. The essays separate accepted records, implementation, past execution and proposals. The explanation supplies no change approval or action permission.

entries.original: An agent begins with a purpose, selected project information and applicable rules and permissions. Reviewed, accepted changes enter saved project knowledge that a later session can inspect.
entries.editorial: An agent starts with purpose, selected information and applicable rules and permission. Reviewed accepted changes enter saved knowledge another session can recover.

entries.original: This sequence explains the intended working loop. Each actual record connection still needs a declared connection rule; placement in this sequence does not create one. Essay 08 explains which parts have operational evidence. Experience can also lead to reflection, a proposed lesson, later use and an assessment of whether it helped.
entries.editorial: This sequence describes the intended work loop. Actual connections need their declared rules. Essay 08 examines operational evidence. Experience can also lead to reflection, advice, later use and a benefit assessment.

entries.original: Which accepted meanings and requirements apply, and who may authorize which consequences within what scope?
entries.editorial: Which meanings and requirements govern here, and who has authority for the proposed consequences within this scope?

entries.original: Each machine agent exists for one session. Project State preserves saved project records and knowledge with their individual statuses. A later agent receives task information and concept maps derived from that state.
entries.editorial: A machine instance belongs to one session. Project State retains knowledge with each record’s standing intact. The next agent obtains task information and connected views from that saved state.

entries.original: These links identify the definitions and sources used by this essay. A source’s older draft label does not override the acceptance recorded for its exact version.
entries.editorial: Follow these links to the exact sources used by the essay. An older draft label leaves standing to the acceptance recorded for that version.

entries.original: This catalog contains the complete current selections from the inspected registries—lists that record definitions, types and permitted connections. Open an entry to read its meaning, required format, acceptance or connection rules. Search by everyday explanation, term, exact identity or contract text.
entries.editorial: The catalog includes the complete inspected registry selections. Open an entry for meaning, format, acceptance or connection rules. Search by everyday explanation, term, identity or exact contract text.

entries.original: The summaries introduce each entry. Exact statements, technical references and original source links remain available inside it. See the reading guide for status and field explanations.
entries.editorial: The summary gives you a starting point. Exact statements, technical references and original links remain inside each entry. The reading guide explains status and field names.

entries.original: Acceptance comes from the recorded decisions and registry selection. An exact version can be accepted while its original name still contains “candidate.” Acceptance of a contract, the state of a particular subject and activation of software are separate facts.
entries.editorial: Use recorded decisions and registry selection to establish acceptance, even when a name retains “candidate.” A contract’s acceptance, a subject’s state and software activation answer separate questions.

entries.original: A definition states what a term means and where that meaning applies. Open an entry for a short introduction, then its exact governing statement.
entries.editorial: A definition gives a term meaning and scope. Begin with the introduction, then inspect the exact governing statement.

entries.original: An artifact is a recorded item, such as a work assignment or observation. Its type contract states the requirements for that kind of item; its schema supplies machine-readable structural rules.
entries.editorial: An artifact records something such as an assignment or observation. Its type contract governs that kind of record, and its schema states machine-readable structural requirements.

entries.original: These keys are required at the selected schema level. Nested fields, alternatives and referenced rules remain in the full schema.
entries.editorial: These are the required keys at the selected schema level. Read the full schema for nested fields, alternatives and referenced rules before judging a complete record.

entries.original: This pattern is one declared ordered pair. A complete connection needs exact endpoints and every applicable contract requirement. Other permitted pairs are listed below.
entries.editorial: This is one declared ordered pair. An actual connection needs exact endpoints and the full contract, including qualifiers. The other permitted pairs are listed below.

entries.original: An endpoint is the thing at either end of a connection. These entries link each permitted kind to its record format and connection rules.
entries.editorial: Endpoints are the subjects at either end of a connection. These entries identify permitted kinds, their formats and connection rules.

entries.original: The three governance lenses are authority, provenance and lifecycle. These seven record facets describe separate matters within the wider model: status does not determine evidence confidence, and an owner’s commitment does not prove a claim.
entries.editorial: Authority, provenance and lifecycle are the three governance questions. The seven facets here record other distinct properties. Status leaves evidence confidence separate, and commitment supplies no proof of a claim.

entries.original: These versions were accepted but are outside the inspected current selection. They remain in the captured registry, allowing earlier meanings and references to be examined.
entries.editorial: These accepted versions are outside current selection. The captured registry preserves them so earlier meanings and references stay inspectable.

entries.original: These accepted contracts are outside the inspected current selection. Their historical listing is separate from the unaccepted proposals retained in the registry.
entries.editorial: These contracts were accepted and are now outside current selection. That history differs from proposals awaiting acceptance.

entries.original: A descriptor is a registry entry describing a type. A contract binding selects the requirements for a record kind or a section of a shared schema. The snapshot selects 114 accepted descriptors and seven additional bindings to shared schema sections, giving 121 current contract bindings.
entries.editorial: A descriptor describes a type. A binding selects requirements for a record kind or shared schema section. This snapshot has 114 selected accepted descriptors and seven further shared-schema bindings, totaling 121 bindings.

entries.editorial: The seven earlier unaccepted descriptor proposals are a different set from the seven current shared-schema bindings. The inventory retains exact counts and field names so you can inspect the distinction.

entries.original: The essays combine registry entries with selected records about governance, integration, acceptance, implemented software, formal analysis and planned work. The research package preserves 484 source files as captured on 8 October 2026, with content fingerprints to identify them. The catalog covers the inspected registry selections; the essays examine the sources relevant to their eight subjects. These records do not establish that the ontology covers the whole repository.
entries.editorial: The research package captures 484 source files from 8 October 2026, with content fingerprints. Essays combine selected registry entries with governance, integration, acceptance, implementation, assurance and planning records. Catalog coverage and whole-repository ontology coverage are different claims.

entries.original: The publications below help explain particular ideas. A comparison does not establish that the Lab implements the publication’s approach, complies with a standard or reproduces a study’s results. Reports of past validation describe the captured evidence; implementation checks were not rerun for this writing task.
entries.editorial: The publications explain particular mechanisms. Comparisons establish neither Lab implementation, standards compliance nor reproduced results. Past validation reports retain their captured scope; this editorial work reruns no implementation suite.

entries.original: A provenance model records entities, activities and participants: what existed, what was done and who was involved. It helps explain tracing a Lab record to its origins; the comparison grants no Lab authority.
entries.editorial: Provenance vocabulary identifies what existed, which activity produced it and who participated. It helps follow a Lab record to its origins while leaving authority to separate records.

entries.original: Attribute-based access control evaluates a requesting participant, the target, the requested operation and relevant conditions. It helps explain actor permissions, one part of the Lab’s broader authority model.
entries.editorial: Attribute-based access control considers requester, subject, action and conditions. Actor permission is one question within the Lab’s broader authority model.

entries.original: Least privilege means granting only the permissions needed for the task. Checking access at each use helps explain why delegation has limits and why previous permission does not settle every later action.
entries.editorial: Least privilege limits grants to the task. Checking access on each use explains why an earlier permission needs reconsideration before later actions.

entries.original: SHACL describes constraints on graph data, such as which fields and connections a node may have. It provides a comparison for structural validation; these essays do not establish that the Lab implements SHACL.
entries.editorial: SHACL declares constraints on graph fields and connections. It helps explain structural validation, without establishing that the Lab implements it.

entries.original: Event sourcing preserves changes as events and reconstructs state from their history. This helps explain replay and derived state. The Lab also records the authority for governed changes.
entries.editorial: Event sourcing retains changes and reconstructs state from history. The Lab separately records the authority behind governed changes.

entries.original: A bounded context defines where a particular model and vocabulary apply. It helps explain how the same word can have different scoped meanings and why connections between contexts need explicit rules.
entries.editorial: A Bounded Context establishes where a model’s vocabulary applies. The same word can have different scoped meanings, with connections between models needing explicit rules.

entries.original: This simulation studies agents using observations, retrieved memories, reflections and plans. It provides an example of external memory architecture; its results do not establish business reliability or Lab conformance.
entries.editorial: The study examines agents using observations, retrieved memories, reflections and plans in simulation. It provides an external-memory precedent within that scope, without establishing business reliability or Lab conformance.

entries.original: A proof checker can establish a formal result about a stated theorem. Whether that theorem captures the intended real-world meaning is a separate question. The essays preserve this distinction when discussing formal assurance.
entries.editorial: A checker can verify a formal theorem. Relating that theorem to the intended meaning is another obligation. The assurance discussion keeps both questions visible.

entries.original: The editorial method emphasizes a central contribution, the reader’s existing knowledge and a logical progression. Those ideas inform the structure of each essay.
entries.editorial: The editorial method asks for a central contribution, attention to what readers know and a logical progression. Those questions informed the essay structure.

entries.original: The proposed module describes authority mainly as decision rights. Accepted definitions also govern meanings, record requirements and permitted connections.
entries.editorial: The proposed module emphasizes decision rights. Accepted definitions also govern meaning, record requirements and connections, so authority needs that broader reading.

entries.original: The essays explain the broader accepted model. Revising the proposed module requires its own review.
entries.editorial: The essays read the accepted model broadly. A revised module still needs its own review.

entries.original: The accepted local software uses an earlier selection of accepted records. A proposed successor selects the later Project State—the project’s saved records and knowledge—and has a captured report of passing checks. The successor still needs separate acceptance.
entries.editorial: The admitted local software uses an earlier source selection. A successor proposes later Project State and has a captured validation report. Accepting that update is still a separate step.

entries.original: The essays distinguish which source records the software selects, which implementation is accepted and what has been exercised.
entries.editorial: Read source selection, implementation acceptance and observed execution as separate facts.

entries.original: The software documentation reports older references that cannot be matched to the selected versions. Replacing their names would not resolve those missing bindings.
entries.editorial: Some older references remain unresolved against selected versions. Renaming them leaves the missing binding to be established.

entries.original: The explanations keep these missing references and their limits visible when describing graph queries.
entries.editorial: The graph-query explanations preserve those unresolved references and the resulting limits.

entries.original: The captured coverage report lists 183 current definition identities. Three have source-linked partial pilot translations, and eight have source-linked notes on the formal foundation. It reports zero verified proofs covering whole definitions.
entries.editorial: The report covers 183 identities, with three source-linked partial pilot translations and eight source-linked foundation notes. It reports zero verified whole-definition proofs.

entries.original: The essays explain non-collapse—finding cases that distinguish meanings—as one assurance method. They make no claim of proven global consistency or complete proof coverage.
entries.editorial: Non-collapse looks for cases distinguishing meanings. The essays claim neither proven global consistency nor complete proof coverage.

entries.original: The ontology import contains 21 packages, and the local software selects particular source records. Their manifests identify bounded source sets. These records do not establish coverage of every current repository object or the existence of a continuously running service.
entries.editorial: The ontology import has 21 packages and the runtime selects bounded sources. Their manifests supply those boundaries. They establish neither coverage of all current objects nor a continuously running service.

entries.original: Read a graph result relative to its declared sources and the question it was constructed to answer.
entries.editorial: Read the graph against its source set and the question the view was built to answer.

entries.original: References from the accepted implementation to a capability do not establish a separately adopted Capability Realization Binding—the record selecting how that capability will be delivered—or a declared realizes connection.
entries.editorial: A runtime’s capability reference still leaves adoption of a Capability Realization Binding and declaration of a realizes connection to their own records.

entries.original: The essays distinguish an association, acceptance of implementation, adoption for a capability, activation and observed benefit.
entries.editorial: Association, implementation acceptance, capability adoption, activation and observed benefit each need a distinct account.

entries.original: The selected definition’s governing wording concerns a concept that requires a governed information view. Its name alone does not establish a formal contract for mapping source data into a projection.
entries.editorial: The governing definition concerns a concept requiring a governed information view. Its name alone supplies no additional formal projection-mapping contract.

entries.original: The library retains the exact governing statement and does not invent additional requirements from the term’s name.
entries.editorial: The library preserves the exact statement rather than adding requirements inferred from its name.

entries.original: The accepted local foundation is distinct from the proposed work needed for repeatable operation, integration, ontology coverage and a usable product. Stable-release prerequisites remain separate.
entries.editorial: The admitted local foundation leaves repeatable operation, integration, scoped ontology coverage and usable-product work to the proposed roadmap. Stable release has its own prerequisites.

entries.original: The essays explain the accepted foundation and the remaining stages without presenting a plan as an achieved outcome.
entries.editorial: The essays show the foundation and open stages. A plan remains a plan until evidence establishes its results.

entries.original: Each essay develops one argument and explains its technical vocabulary in context. The business examples make the concepts concrete; the catalog retains the full technical records. Short definition introductions are editorial aids beside the exact governing statements. Mensh and Kording’s paper informs the focus on a central contribution and what a reader needs to understand it. Ten simple rules for structuring papers .
entries.editorial: Each essay develops one argument with vocabulary explained in context. Cases make the ideas concrete; the catalog preserves full records. The short introductions are explanatory aids beside governing statements. Mensh and Kording inform the focus on contribution and the reader’s understanding.

entries.editorial: For source tracking, use the source list, catalog data, editorial notes and series outline.

entries.editorial: Browse the sections or use your browser’s Find command. Interactive search needs JavaScript.

entries.editorial: Follow the Northstar incident from the agent’s investigation through assessment, change decisions and a later use of the lesson.

entries.original: Examine which rules apply, where information came from and how it may change. Definitions, formats, policies and decisions have distinct roles.
entries.editorial: Begin with three questions: which rules apply, where did the information come from, and what would allow a change? Definitions, formats, policies and decisions answer different parts of those questions.

entries.original: Choose a response to a need and a success test. Record the product outcome, selected software and particular project effort separately.
entries.editorial: Choose a response to the need and say how you’ll judge success. Then distinguish the product outcome, the software selected to deliver it and the project doing the work.

entries.editorial: The session starts from saved Project State, through selected task information and a view of relevant connections. Its profile, assignment and permissions establish how it works. When the session ends, its machine instance and working memory end too.

entries.original: Record what happened, examine possible failure patterns and test uncertain explanations. Advice for later work needs recorded use and an assessment of its benefit.
entries.editorial: Save what happened. Examine possible failure patterns and test explanations you’re unsure about. A lesson for later work needs more than a place in the library: record where it was used and examine whether it helped.

entries.editorial: Each point in the graph represents a particular record version. A connection represents an existing relationship or a declared local meaning. Separate histories let us reconstruct the recorded state selected for the view.

entries.editorial: Session 12 receives a Work Assignment. The owner separately delegates 30 minutes to inspect saved material and prepare material for review. The assignment supplies the job; the delegation supplies its permission.

entries.editorial: Method 2 compares identifiers in snapshot S1 and output E12, using completeness definition 1.0.0. The Evidence Set preserves what the comparison found, so a Failure Assessment can examine the result within that scope.

entries.editorial: The service owner has accepted version 1.0.0 for these customer-data export assessments. So the agent has a specific criterion to work from: every required identifier selected by the account, filters and fixed snapshot must appear in the output.

entries.editorial: The authorized owner permits inspection of saved input, output and run logs, comparison of identifiers, saving candidate assessment material and preparing a change proposal. To continue, the delegation must still be current and the task view usable.

entries.editorial: Compare E12 with the identifiers required for Northstar and status = active in S1. Use the account membership and filter values recorded in that snapshot. Otherwise, you’d be comparing different sets.

entries.editorial: If permission expires or is revoked, or the task view becomes unusable, the agent pauses. It also stops before an action outside its scope. Changing source data, activating code and closing the incident each need authority for that particular effect.

entries.editorial: A digest is a digital fingerprint of a file’s contents. It helps us identify the exact file used in the comparison. The fingerprint does not tell us whether the contents, or our conclusion about them, are correct.

entries.editorial: A machine-agent instance belongs to one session. It ends with that session, along with its working memory. The next session recovers continuity from saved Project State, using a Context View prepared for its task and an Ontology View of the relevant concepts and connections.

entries.editorial: Definition 1.0.0 tells the agent what to check. The owner’s delegation permits this investigation. Adopting a fix, activating it and closing the incident each need a decision with the appropriate scope.

entries.editorial: If the owner determines that a change materially alters meaning, scope or semantic requirements, it needs a successor meaning version and explicit owner selection. Changing which rows qualify for an export would be such a change.

entries.editorial: A new machine encoding needs evidence of equivalent meaning, validation and owner selection. Keep the earlier revision identifiable so someone can examine what changed.

entries.editorial: A regenerated view adds no meaning or authority when it uses unchanged canonical input and the exact generator binding, then passes validation. Changing the generator is a separate governed change.

entries.editorial: The incident coordinates the response: who is accountable, what gets communicated, how recovery is assessed and when closure is justified. Its response remains open. The repair project and investigation have their own states.

entries.editorial: Read how Craft fits into the Lab, then follow its capacity-decision example. It takes a definition into a typed software model, with a separate criterion for acceptance.

entries.editorial: A Ledger keeps an ordered collection under declared rules. An event history adds requirements for retaining prior entries and reconstructing state from them. Those extra requirements matter when we rely on the history to recover a project.

entries.editorial: The definition tells us what Work means. The artifact type specifies the record format. The particular Work record describes Northstar’s omission investigation. These arrows show how the roles fit together. Permitted connections still come from their declared contracts.

entries.editorial: Compare the two models in the Craft article. If a software Rule implements a governing Lab definition, record that correspondence explicitly and version it under the applicable contract. A shared name does not establish the binding.

entries.original: Cloudflare's July 2019 outage shows why the checked properties matter. A firewall rule exhausted CPU through excessive regular-expression backtracking. Its postmortem describes a removed resource protection, a test suite that did not detect excessive CPU consumption and a routine rule rollout that went global without staging. The change passed the existing delivery process, but that process did not establish the needed performance and rollout properties. Cloudflare's postmortem
entries.editorial: Cloudflare’s July 2019 outage shows what an existing check can miss. A firewall rule exhausted CPU through excessive regular-expression backtracking. The postmortem describes a removed resource protection, tests that missed excessive CPU consumption and a routine rollout that reached the world without staging. The delivery process accepted the change. It had not established the performance and rollout properties the service needed.

entries.editorial: For Craft, we need to state the obligations and identify which checks address them. A compiler or artifact comparison examines selected structural and behavioral contracts. Resource limits and rollout safety need their own explicit constraints and evidence.
